instructions.title: Pre-Drive Vehicle Check
instructions.whereDetailed: Start at the driver door and walk clockwise so you always finish where you started.
instructions.description: The walk-around and cab check that happens before every single departure, however short the drive.
instructions.warnings: Never skip this because the drive is short. Most damage happens on the first hundred metres — an open locker, a connected cable, a step still out.
instructions.equipment: Tyre gauge, torch
instructions.preparations: Everyone out of the vehicle and standing clear before you start the walk.
steps: Mains hook-up cable unplugged, coiled and stowed in its locker.
Gas turned off at the bottle.
All external lockers closed and locked — push each one.
Step retracted and locked.
Awning fully rolled in and arms latched.
TV aerial down, satellite dish stowed, roof vents closed.
Tyres: quick visual for bulges or flats, pressures if not checked this week.
Walk the full circle once more looking underneath for chocks, blocks and levelling ramps.
In the cab: mirrors set, handbrake, seatbelts on for everyone, dash warning lights clear.
instructions.afterUse: Note anything you found out of place — a locker you keep forgetting is worth a sticker.
instructions.notes: The single most useful habit: always walk the same direction. Your eye learns the pattern and spots the exception.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Securing the Interior Before Driving
instructions.description: Making the living space road-safe so nothing becomes a projectile.
instructions.warnings: An unsecured object in a hard stop travels at the speed you were driving. Heavy items low, always.
instructions.preparations: Do this before the outside walk-around so the last thing you do is close the door.
steps: Fridge door latched on its travel catch.
All overhead lockers pushed shut until they click.
Loose items off worktops and tables — into a drawer, a sink, or the footwell.
Heavy things stowed low and forward, never in high lockers.
Bathroom door latched, shower screen secured.
Roof lights and skylights closed and locked.
Any hanging item taken down.
Pull the sliding door / internal doors onto their catches.
instructions.notes: A folded tea towel in the sink stops crockery rattling for the whole trip.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Reversing and Parking the RV
instructions.where: Arrival point, pitch or parking space
instructions.description: A repeatable method for getting a long vehicle into a tight space without a shouting match.
instructions.warnings: If you cannot see your helper in the mirror, stop. No exceptions — that is the rule that prevents the accident.
instructions.equipment: Phone or radios, reversing camera if fitted
instructions.preparations: Both of you agree the hand signals BEFORE you start, and agree that a raised flat palm means stop immediately.
steps: Stop and get out. Walk the space you are reversing into and look up as well as down — branches, wires, roof boxes.
Agree the final position and which side is tight.
Helper stands at the rear corner on the tight side, always visible in your mirror.
Set the mirrors down slightly so you can see the rear wheels.
Reverse in short bursts, stopping between each.
Steer to the mirror showing the problem — turn the wheel towards the side you want the back to go.
If you lose sight of the helper, stop and wait.
When in position, handbrake on, then get out and check clearance all round before switching off.
instructions.afterUse: Note the pitch orientation for levelling.
instructions.notes: Slow is smooth and smooth is fast. Nobody has ever regretted reversing too slowly.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Driving in Strong Crosswinds
instructions.where: On the road — exposed sections, bridges, open plains
instructions.description: How to handle a big flat-sided vehicle when the weather turns.
instructions.warnings: The dangerous moment is not the gust itself — it is the sudden loss of wind when you pass behind a lorry or into a cutting, and your correction is still applied.
steps: Slow down early. Speed multiplies every wind effect.
Both hands on the wheel, thumbs outside the rim.
Move to the centre of your lane to buy room on both sides.
Anticipate gaps in shelter: bridge ends, gateways, gaps between buildings.
When overtaking or being overtaken by a lorry, expect a push away then a pull towards it.
Make small, early corrections rather than large late ones.
If it becomes hard work, stop. A service area for an hour costs nothing.
instructions.notes: Check the forecast for wind speed as routinely as you check for rain. Above about 50 km/h of gust, plan a shorter day.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Mountain Descents — Engine Braking
instructions.description: Getting a heavy vehicle down a long descent without cooking the brakes.
instructions.warnings: Brake fade is silent until it is total. If you smell hot brakes, stop in a safe place and let them cool for at least 20 minutes — do not apply the handbrake on hot discs.
instructions.preparations: At the top of the pass, stop, check the descent profile, and drop a gear before you start rather than after.
steps: Select a low gear at the top — the same gear you would need to climb it.
Let the engine hold the speed. The rule of thumb: if you need constant brake, you are a gear too high.
Brake firmly and briefly to shed speed, then release fully. Never ride the brake pedal.
Use any exhaust brake or retarder if fitted.
Keep a very large gap to the vehicle in front.
Pull in at designated cooling points on long descents.
Watch temperature and any warning lights the whole way down.
instructions.afterUse: At the bottom, let the brakes cool before parking on a slope. Chock the wheels rather than relying on a hot handbrake.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Refuelling Routine
instructions.description: Fuelling a tall, long vehicle without damage or drama.
instructions.warnings: Check the canopy height BEFORE entering the forecourt. Reversing off a forecourt is far harder than driving past it.
steps: Approach slowly, check the height limit sign and the roof clearance.
Choose a pump with a clear exit — ideally one you can drive straight out of.
Note which side your filler is on before you commit to a lane.
Turn off gas and any appliances before fuelling.
Fill, and check the fuel type twice. Diesel vehicles: check twice again.
Replace the cap properly and hear it click.
Take the receipt, note the odometer and litres.
Pull forward clear of the pump before doing anything else.
instructions.afterUse: Log the fill in a note — litres, price and odometer. Fuel consumption drifting upwards is an early warning of a mechanical problem.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Tyre Pressure Check
instructions.description: Checking and setting pressures on a heavy vehicle where pressures matter more than on a car.
instructions.warnings: Check cold — before driving, or at least three hours after. A warm tyre reads high and will leave you under-inflated.
instructions.equipment: Accurate gauge, compressor able to reach the RV pressures, valve extensions if fitted
steps: Find your plated pressures — they are on the vehicle plate, not the tyre sidewall.
Note whether you are running loaded or unloaded pressures.
Remove the valve cap, press the gauge on squarely and read.
Inflate or deflate to the plated figure.
Repeat for every wheel including any inner rears and the spare.
While at each wheel, look at the tread depth and sidewalls for cracks or bulges.
Check the DOT date code — tyres over five years old need inspecting, over ten replacing regardless of tread.
Replace all valve caps.
instructions.notes: Under-inflation is the single biggest cause of RV tyre failure. Ten minutes a week is the cheapest insurance on the vehicle.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Route Planning — Heights, Weights and Tolls
instructions.description: Planning a route that a 3.5-tonne, 3-metre-tall vehicle can actually complete.
instructions.warnings: Car satnavs do not know your height or weight. Never follow one blindly into a village.
instructions.equipment: Vehicle dimensions written down, motorhome-aware navigation app
steps: Write your real height, length, width and laden weight on a card for the cab.
Set those dimensions in the navigation app before planning.
Check the route for low bridges, weight limits and width restrictions.
Look at the last two kilometres of each destination — that is where the trouble is.
Check toll classes for your height and axle count; some are charged by height over 3m.
Identify fuel stops with easy access and overnight options if the day overruns.
Note any environmental / low-emission zones needing a sticker.
Have a plan B for the day if the weather turns.
instructions.notes: Satellite view of the final approach and the campsite entrance is worth five minutes of anyone's time.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Night Driving Setup
instructions.description: Preparing the cab and yourself for driving after dark.
instructions.warnings: Fatigue arrives faster at night and you will underestimate it. Plan to stop rather than plan to push on.
steps: Clean the windscreen inside and out — inside film is what causes the starburst glare.
Dim the dashboard and any screens to the lowest readable level.
Turn off interior habitation lights so nothing reflects in the glass.
Check headlight aim is set for the load you are carrying.
Set a stop time before you start, and honour it.
Keep the cab cool — warmth makes you drowsy.
Increase your following distance well beyond the daytime gap.
instructions.afterUse: On arrival, do not attempt a difficult reverse in the dark if you can avoid it. Park easy, reposition in the morning.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Filling the Fresh Water Tank
instructions.description: Taking on drinking water cleanly.
instructions.warnings: Only ever use the dedicated fresh water hose, and never let its end touch the ground or go near the waste point.
instructions.equipment: Food-grade fresh water hose, tap adapters, inline filter
instructions.preparations: Check the tap is marked drinking water. If it is not marked, treat it as non-potable.
steps: Take out the fresh hose — the one that is stored separately from everything else.
Flush the tap for 30 seconds before connecting.
Connect the inline filter and the hose.
Run water through the hose for 20 seconds before putting it in the filler.
Open the fresh water filler cap and insert the hose.
Fill, watching the gauge — and remember every 100 litres is 100 kg of payload.
Stop before full if you have a long drive; carry only the water you need.
Cap the filler, drain the hose fully, coil it and stow it in its own bag.
instructions.afterUse: Dry the hose ends before stowing. A wet coiled hose grows things.
instructions.maintenance: Sanitise the system twice a year — see instruction 110.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Sanitising the Fresh Water System
instructions.description: The twice-yearly clean of tank, pipes and taps.
instructions.warnings: Follow the dose on the product exactly. Too strong damages seals; too weak does nothing at all.
instructions.equipment: Water system sanitiser, fresh hose, spare drinking water
instructions.preparations: Do this when you have half a day and access to a drain. Plan it for the start and end of the season.
steps: Drain the tank and the system completely, including the water heater.
Refill the tank with fresh water and add the sanitiser at the stated dose.
Run every tap — hot and cold, kitchen, bathroom, shower and outside shower — until you smell the solution at each.
Leave to stand for the time the product states, usually a few hours.
Drain the whole system down again.
Refill with clean fresh water and run every tap through until no smell or taste remains.
Repeat the rinse if any taste lingers.
Replace the inline filter cartridge with a new one.
instructions.afterUse: Note the date. Two per year, start and end of season, is a good rhythm.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Emptying the Grey Water Tank
instructions.where: Grey waste valve, campsite disposal point
instructions.description: Getting rid of sink and shower water responsibly.
instructions.warnings: Never empty grey water onto the ground or into a storm drain, however clean you think it is. It contains grease and detergent.
instructions.equipment: Waste hose if fitted, gloves
steps: Position over the disposal point, or connect the waste hose to it.
Check the drain will take the flow before you open anything.
Open the grey valve fully and let it run.
When it slows to a trickle, close and reopen once to shift anything sitting in the pipe.
Close the valve firmly.
Rinse the outlet and the hose with clean water — never the fresh hose.
Stow the waste hose in its own dedicated box, away from the fresh hose.
instructions.afterUse: A cupful of biological cleaner down the sink afterwards keeps the tank from smelling.
instructions.maintenance: Every few months, fill the grey tank with water and a tank cleaner, drive a short distance to slosh it, then drain.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Emptying the Black Water Cassette
instructions.description: The toilet cassette routine — the job nobody enjoys, done properly so it takes five minutes.
instructions.warnings: Only ever empty into a proper chemical disposal point. Never a normal drain, never a public toilet unless it is signed for it.
instructions.equipment: Disposable gloves, toilet fluid, rinse water
instructions.preparations: Empty before it is completely full — a full cassette is heavy and hard to handle.
steps: Put gloves on. This is not the moment for stoicism.
Check the blade valve is closed, then release and withdraw the cassette from its hatch.
Wheel or carry it to the chemical disposal point.
Position over the point, hold the vent button in as you pour to avoid glugging and splashing.
Rinse the cassette with clean water two or three times, pouring out each time.
Add the correct dose of toilet fluid and about a litre of water to cover the blade.
Slide the cassette back in and lock the hatch.
Wash hands properly, then wash them again.
instructions.afterUse: Rinse the disposal point after yourself — leave it as you would like to find it.
instructions.maintenance: Once a season, clean the blade seal and lubricate it with the manufacturer's spray. A dry seal is what starts leaks.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Water Pump Priming and Air Bleed
instructions.description: What to do when the pump runs but no water arrives, or the taps splutter.
instructions.warnings: Do not let the pump run dry for more than a few seconds — it is the quickest way to destroy it.
steps: Confirm there is actually water in the tank. Check the gauge and, if in doubt, look.
Turn the pump on at the control panel.
Open the tap physically highest and furthest from the pump first.
Let it run and splutter until the flow is steady — this pushes the air out.
Work back through the other taps one at a time, hot and cold.
Include the shower and any outside shower.
If nothing comes at all, switch the pump off and check the inline filter for a blockage or an airlock.
Check for a closed drain valve left open from winterising.
instructions.notes: A tap that splutters only on hot usually means air trapped in the water heater, not a pump fault.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Winterising the Water System
instructions.description: Draining everything down so a hard frost cannot split a pipe.
instructions.warnings: Water expands as it freezes and will split a pipe, a pump or a water heater. A missed drain point is an expensive repair.
instructions.preparations: Do this before the first frost is forecast, not after.
steps: Turn the pump off and switch off the water heater.
Open the water heater drain valve and let it empty fully.
Open every low-point drain valve you have — list them once and keep the list.
Open every tap, hot and cold, and leave them open in the mid position.
Empty the fresh tank completely.
Empty the grey tank and leave its valve open.
Empty, rinse and dry the toilet cassette, and leave it out with the cap loose.
Run the pump for a couple of seconds only to clear it, then leave the system open.
Leave shower heads hanging down to drain.
instructions.afterUse: Leave a note on the steering wheel listing which valves are open, so recommissioning is not guesswork.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Water Filter Replacement
instructions.description: Changing the inline drinking water filter cartridge.
instructions.warnings: An old filter is worse than no filter — it becomes a place for bacteria to live.
instructions.equipment: Correct replacement cartridge, filter housing spanner
steps: Turn the pump off and open a tap to release pressure.
Place a bowl under the housing — there will be water in it.
Unscrew the housing and remove the old cartridge.
Wash the housing out with clean water; do not use detergent.
Check the O-ring, clean it and smear it with silicone grease.
Fit the new cartridge the correct way round.
Screw the housing back, hand-tight plus a nudge with the spanner.
Turn the pump on and run the nearest tap until the water runs clear.
instructions.afterUse: Write the date on the housing with a marker, or on the filter itself.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Shower Routine — Water Saving
instructions.description: Getting properly clean on a fraction of a normal shower.
instructions.warnings: Watch the grey tank as well as the fresh — running out of somewhere to put it is the more common surprise.
instructions.preparations: Have everything to hand before you start: towel, soap, shampoo.
steps: Turn the water heater on 20 minutes ahead and off again before you shower.
Wet down for about 20 seconds, then stop the water.
Soap and shampoo with the water off.
Rinse in one continuous pass, top to bottom.
Squeegee the walls and screen while still in there.
Open the roof vent and leave the door open afterwards.
Wipe out the tray so no standing water is left.
instructions.afterUse: A quick wipe of the tray each time is what stops the bathroom smelling by day four.
instructions.notes: Two people can wash comfortably on around 20 litres this way.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Connecting to Campsite Mains (Hook-Up)
instructions.description: Getting mains power on safely, in the right order.
instructions.warnings: Always connect at the vehicle first and the bollard last, and disconnect in the reverse order. Never leave a live cable end on the ground.
instructions.equipment: Hook-up cable, continental adapters, polarity tester
steps: Uncoil the cable completely — a coiled cable under load gets hot.
Plug into the RV inlet first.
Plug into the bollard socket second and switch it on.
Test polarity with the tester; if reversed, use a reversing adapter or do not use the supply.
Check the amperage the pitch supplies — often 6A or 10A, not 16A.
Switch on the RV consumer unit and check the RCD trips and resets.
Work out your load budget: a kettle and a heater together will trip a 6A supply.
Route the cable so nobody trips and it is not under a wheel.
instructions.afterUse: On departure, switch off at the bollard, unplug bollard end first, then the vehicle end.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Leisure Battery Health Check
instructions.description: Knowing whether your battery is healthy or quietly dying.
instructions.warnings: Lead-acid batteries give off hydrogen. No naked flames, no smoking, and ventilate the compartment.
instructions.equipment: Multimeter, distilled water if serviceable cells, terminal grease
steps: Check the resting voltage with everything off and nothing charging, ideally after a few hours: 12.7V is full, 12.2V is about half, below 12.0V is flat.
Look at the terminals for corrosion; clean and grease them if furred.
Check the terminals are tight — a loose terminal mimics a dead battery.
On serviceable batteries, check electrolyte level and top up with distilled water only.
Watch the voltage under load: turn on a heavy load and see how far it drops and how fast it recovers.
Check the charger is actually reaching absorption voltage when on hook-up.
Note the battery age — most leisure batteries are tired at five years.
instructions.afterUse: Record the resting voltage each month. The trend tells you far more than any single reading.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Solar Panel Check and Clean
instructions.description: Keeping the panels producing what they should.
instructions.warnings: Do not walk on the roof unless it is rated for it. Use a ladder and reach, or a long-handled brush from the ground.
instructions.equipment: Soft brush, clean water, ladder
instructions.preparations: Do it early or late — never on a hot panel, and never with cold water on hot glass.
steps: Check the controller output on a bright day and note the figure.
Inspect the panel glass for dirt, bird mess, leaf litter and sap.
Wash with clean water and a soft brush only. No detergent, no abrasives.
Check the mounting feet and the sealant round them for lifting or cracking.
Check the cable gland where the wiring enters the roof for perished sealant.
Look for any shading — a new roof box or aerial can cost you a surprising amount of output.
Recheck the controller output afterwards and compare.
instructions.afterUse: Note the before and after figures. A panel that stays low after cleaning has a wiring or controller issue.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Inverter Use and Load Limits
instructions.description: Running mains appliances off the battery without flattening it or tripping out.
instructions.warnings: High-draw heating appliances — kettle, toaster, hairdryer, heater — will empty a leisure battery in minutes. Know your numbers before you plug in.
steps: Check the inverter's continuous rating, not its peak rating.
Work out the draw: watts divided by 12 gives roughly the amps taken from the battery.
Check the battery state of charge before starting anything heavy.
Switch the inverter on, then the appliance — never the other way round.
Run one heavy appliance at a time.
Watch the battery voltage while running; stop if it drops below about 12.0V.
Switch the appliance off, then the inverter. Leaving it idling drains the battery all night.
instructions.notes: A 2000W kettle pulls roughly 170A from a 12V battery. That is why campsites have hook-up.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Gas Bottle Change
instructions.description: Swapping an empty gas bottle for a full one.
instructions.warnings: Outside only, no naked flame anywhere near, nobody smoking, and every appliance off before you start. Gas fittings are usually left-hand thread.
instructions.equipment: Spanner, new bottle, spare washer, leak-detection spray
steps: Turn every gas appliance off inside, and the isolation valve too.
Close the valve on the bottle you are removing.
Undo the regulator connection — remember most are left-hand thread, so it undoes clockwise.
Lift the empty out and cap it.
Stand the full bottle in place and strap it in before connecting anything.
Check the sealing washer is present and in good condition; replace it if flattened or cracked.
Connect the regulator and tighten — firm, not brutal.
Open the bottle valve slowly and spray every joint with leak spray. Bubbles mean stop and redo it.
Open the isolation valve and light one appliance to purge the air.
instructions.afterUse: Write the changeover date somewhere. It tells you your real gas consumption.
instructions.maintenance: Regulators have a service life of about ten years — check the date stamped on yours.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Gas Leak Check
instructions.description: Testing the gas system for leaks — a safety check, not an optional one.
instructions.warnings: Never test with a flame. If you smell gas at any point: bottle off, doors and windows open, everybody out, no switches touched.
instructions.equipment: Leak detection spray or soapy water, gas alarm
steps: Turn all appliances off but leave the bottle valve and isolation valve open.
Spray every joint from the bottle onwards: regulator, hose, isolation valve, and each appliance connection.
Watch for bubbles growing over about 30 seconds.
Check the flexible hose along its whole length for cracking, hardening or chafing.
Check the hose date — most need replacing every five years regardless of appearance.
If your system has a bubble tester, use it as the manufacturer describes.
Test the gas alarm with its test button.
Close everything down and note the date of the check.
instructions.afterUse: A professional gas safety check as part of the annual habitation service does not replace this monthly look.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Fridge Changeover (Gas / Mains / 12V)
instructions.description: Running the three-way fridge on the right power source for the situation.
instructions.warnings: Turn the fridge off gas before entering a fuel station, a ferry, or a tunnel where it is prohibited.
steps: On hook-up: run on mains. It is the cheapest and does not use your gas or battery.
Driving: run on 12V, which only works with the engine running and will not cool from warm.
Off-grid and stationary: run on gas.
Pre-cool on mains for several hours before you load it — a three-way fridge cools slowly.
Check the vent covers outside are clear.
On gas, check the flame has actually lit; many failures are silent.
On arrival, switch from 12V back to mains or gas straight away or you will flatten the battery.
instructions.notes: Ventilation is everything with an absorption fridge. In hot weather, shade the outside vents and it will work far better.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Heating System Start-Up
instructions.description: Bringing the heating on for the first time in the season, or after a period unused.
instructions.warnings: A heater unused for months can burn off dust and smell for the first few minutes — ventilate. If the smell is of gas rather than dust, shut it down.
steps: Check the external flue and intake are clear of leaves, insects and nests.
Check every internal vent and outlet is unobstructed — not behind a cushion or a bag.
Check the gas supply is on and the bottle is not empty.
Set the thermostat well above room temperature so it fires and stays firing.
Start it and stand by for the first five minutes.
Check warm air actually arrives at every outlet.
If it has a water heater function, check that too but only with the system filled.
Set the thermostat back to a normal setting.
instructions.afterUse: Note anything that did not work while you are still somewhere you can get it fixed.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Air Conditioning Use
instructions.description: Getting the most cooling for the least power.
instructions.warnings: Most roof air conditioners need a full 16A hook-up. On a 6A pitch it will trip as soon as anything else switches on.
steps: Close all windows, roof lights and the door before starting.
Pull blinds and curtains on the sunny side — shading beats cooling.
Park nose-in to the sun so the smallest area is exposed if you have the choice.
Start on high to pull the temperature down, then drop to low to hold it.
Set a target only a few degrees below outside; chasing 18°C in 35°C heat just burns power.
Use the recirculate setting once the space is cool.
Check the condensate drain is clear and dripping outside.
instructions.maintenance: Clean or replace the intake filters at the start of every season — a blocked filter halves the output.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Arrival and Pitch Set-Up
instructions.description: The full arrival routine, in the order that avoids doing anything twice.
instructions.preparations: Walk the pitch first: slope, soft ground, overhanging branches, where the bollard and the drain are.
steps: Position the vehicle for levelling and for which side the awning and door are on.
Level the RV — see instruction 127 — before anything else, because everything after depends on it.
Handbrake on, chocks in, engine off.
Connect the mains hook-up (117).
Turn the gas on and set the fridge to mains or gas (123).
Extend the step and check it is solid on the ground.
Deploy the awning if the weather is settled (128).
Fill the fresh water if needed (109), and check where the waste points are.
Set up outside: chairs, table, mat.
Last: sit down.
instructions.afterUse: Note the pitch number, the bollard number and the wifi code somewhere you will find them.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Levelling the RV
instructions.description: Getting the vehicle level so the fridge works, doors stay put and you do not roll out of bed.
instructions.warnings: Absorption fridges need to be close to level to work at all. Persistent tilt can damage them permanently.
instructions.equipment: Levelling ramps or blocks, spirit level or app, wheel chocks
steps: Park roughly where you want to end up and check the level, side to side first.
Decide which wheels need to come up. Always raise, never dig.
Place the ramps in front of or behind the low-side wheels.
Drive on slowly with someone watching, and stop as soon as level is reached.
Handbrake on, chock the wheels that are NOT on ramps.
Now check front to back and adjust with blocks under the jockey wheel or by repositioning.
Confirm with the level in the doorway and again inside on the floor.
Open and shut the door — if it swings on its own, you are still out.
instructions.notes: Level front to back matters for the shower tray draining; level side to side matters for the fridge.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Awning Deployment
instructions.description: Getting the awning out without damaging it.
instructions.warnings: Never leave an awning out unattended, and never overnight. It takes one gust.
instructions.equipment: Awning pegs, storm straps, tensioner poles
instructions.preparations: Check the forecast for wind and the sky for what is coming. If in doubt, leave it in.
steps: Check overhead for branches and check the ground for where the legs will land.
Wind or pull the awning out slowly, keeping the fabric even.
Set the legs and tension them so the fabric is taut, not drum-tight.
Set one side slightly lower than the other so rain runs off rather than pooling.
Peg the legs down and fit storm straps if there is any wind at all.
Check the fabric is not touching anything that will rub.
Walk under it and look up — any sag is where water will collect.
instructions.afterUse: Check it again after any change in the weather, and before going to bed.
instructions.maintenance: Never roll it away wet for more than a day or two — see 129.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Awning Retraction in Wind
instructions.description: Getting the awning in quickly and safely when the weather turns.
instructions.warnings: A flapping awning can take the side of the vehicle with it. Act early — the moment you are wondering whether to bring it in is the moment to bring it in.
steps: Get everything off the awning and out of the way first — chairs, table, lights.
Two people if at all possible, one at each end.
Release the storm straps and pull the pegs.
Take the tension off the legs and fold them in against the vehicle.
Roll or wind it in steadily, keeping tension on the fabric so it does not billow.
Do not fight a gust — pause between gusts and work in the lulls.
Latch the arms and check the roller is fully home.
Check the fabric is not trapped and the case is closed.
instructions.afterUse: If it went away wet, get it out to dry within a day or two at the next dry opportunity or it will mildew.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Departure — Breaking Down the Pitch
instructions.description: Leaving a pitch in the right order, with nothing left behind.
steps: Empty grey and black waste before you pack anything else — it is easier while still set up (111, 112).
Fill fresh water if you need it for the journey (109).
Bring in and pack the outside furniture, mat and lights.
Retract the awning and latch it (128).
Disconnect the mains: bollard off, bollard end first, then the vehicle end (117).
Gas off at the bottle. Fridge to 12V.
Secure the interior (101).
Retract the step.
Drive off the ramps, then collect ramps and chocks — the most commonly forgotten items on earth.
Walk the pitch in a full circle looking for anything left, including pegs.
Full pre-drive check (100).
instructions.afterUse: Leave the pitch cleaner than you found it.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Making Up the Bed
instructions.description: Converting and making the bed so it is comfortable and quick.
steps: Clear the area and stow anything on the seats.
Slide or fold the boards out and check they are properly located.
Fit the infill cushions and check for gaps — a gap under the small of your back ruins a night.
Fitted sheet on, corners tucked properly.
Duvet or sleeping bags out.
Pillows, and a spare within reach.
Set up a light and a place to put a glass of water.
Check the blinds and blackout are ready.
instructions.afterUse: In the morning, air the bedding before folding it away — condensation collects under a mattress that is put away warm.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Evening Wind-Down Routine
instructions.description: The end-of-day sequence that makes the morning easier.
steps: Awning in if there is any wind forecast overnight (128).
Outside furniture in or secured.
Dishes done and worktops clear.
Check the water level and the waste tank levels so there are no surprises at 7am.
Charge phones and any lights.
Set the heating to its overnight setting.
Crack a roof vent for ventilation (133).
Check the door is locked and the step is in.
Make the bed up (131).

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Ventilation and Condensation Control
instructions.description: Keeping the inside dry — the single biggest factor in whether a vehicle stays healthy.
instructions.warnings: Never block the fixed floor or wall vents. They are there for gas safety as well as damp, and covering them can be lethal.
steps: Leave a roof vent cracked open overnight, every night, in every season.
Cook with the roof vent open and a window ajar.
Wipe condensation off windows in the morning rather than letting it run into the frames.
Open the wardrobe and locker doors during the day to let air move through.
Lift mattresses and cushions regularly so the underside can breathe.
After showering, vent hard for ten minutes (116).
Use a moisture trap in cold weather and empty it when full.
Dry wet coats and boots outside or in the shower, not draped over the seating.
instructions.notes: Two people breathing overnight produce close to a litre of water. It has to go somewhere.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Blackout and Insulation for Cold Nights
instructions.description: Making the vehicle warm and dark enough to sleep properly.
steps: Fit the external or internal cab screens — the windscreen is the biggest heat loss by far.
Close all blinds and curtains, and tuck them against the frame.
Fit thermal blinds to the roof lights.
Lay a rug or mat on the floor.
Keep a gap for ventilation despite all of the above (133).
Set the heating low and steady overnight rather than off and then blasting.
Put a blanket over the duvet rather than turning the heat up.
instructions.afterUse: Take the screens off in the morning to avoid trapping condensation against the glass.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Interior Cleaning Routine
instructions.description: The regular clean that keeps a small space liveable.
instructions.equipment: Small vacuum, microfibre cloths, mild cleaner, bathroom cleaner
steps: Clear all surfaces completely first.
Work top to bottom: lockers, then worktops, then seating, then floor.
Wipe down all surfaces with a mild cleaner — avoid anything abrasive on plastics and acrylic windows.
Clean the acrylic windows with a proper acrylic cleaner and a soft cloth only. Never glass cleaner, never a dry cloth.
Bathroom: toilet, basin, shower tray, mirror.
Kitchen: sink, hob, fridge shelves, and check for anything past its date.
Vacuum including under cushions and in the seat rails.
Shake mats and rugs outside.
Empty the bins.
instructions.notes: Acrylic windows scratch if you look at them wrongly. One dedicated cloth, kept clean, used for nothing else.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Monthly Habitation Check
instructions.description: A structured monthly walk-through of the living systems.
instructions.preparations: Do it on a dry day with good light, and write the results down.
steps: Water: pump, all taps hot and cold, water heater, and check under the sink for drips.
Gas: leak check (122), all appliances light and run properly.
Electrics: hook-up, RCD test, battery voltage (118), all lights, all 12V sockets.
Fridge: runs on all three sources (123).
Heating: fires and heats (124).
Damp: meter or hand check at every known weak point (138).
Seals: eyes over every external seal and joint (137).
Safety: alarms tested (147), extinguisher in date (146), first aid kit stocked (149).
Tyres: pressures and condition (106).
Write the date and anything found in a running log.
instructions.afterUse: Anything found goes onto the Actions list as a to-do straight away, before you forget it.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Seals and Silicone Inspection
instructions.description: Looking at every joint where water could get in.
instructions.warnings: Water ingress is the thing that writes off habitation bodies. Twenty minutes now beats a rebuild later.
instructions.equipment: Torch, ladder, notebook
steps: Work methodically round the vehicle, then the roof, then underneath.
Check every window frame seal for lifting, cracking or gaps.
Check every door and locker frame the same way.
Check the roof: every light, vent, aerial, solar mount and the seam along each edge.
Check the awning rail along its full length.
Press gently on suspect sealant — if it has gone hard or lifted, it is no longer sealing.
Note the location of anything doubtful rather than trying to fix it there and then.
Check the underside for stone damage and any exposed edges.
instructions.afterUse: Book any resealing before the wet season, not during it.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Damp Check
instructions.description: Testing for water ingress before it becomes visible.
instructions.warnings: By the time you can see or smell damp, it has been there a long time. Measure, do not eyeball.
instructions.equipment: Damp meter, torch
steps: Test the same points every time and write the readings down — the trend is the information.
Test the bottom corners of every wall.
Test around every window and roof light, at the frame edge.
Test inside every external locker, especially the lowest edge.
Test around the door frame and under the bed and seating.
Test around the shower and the toilet.
Anything under about 15% is generally fine; 15-25% is worth watching; over 25% needs investigating.
Sniff as well as measure — a musty locker is a real signal.
instructions.afterUse: Compare against last time. A reading that has climbed is more important than a reading that is merely high.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Roof Inspection and Clean
instructions.description: Getting up top safely and checking what you cannot see from the ground.
instructions.warnings: Only walk on the roof if it is explicitly rated for it, and never when wet. Otherwise work from a ladder and reach in sections.
instructions.equipment: Stable ladder, soft brush, long-handled brush, hose
steps: Set the ladder on firm level ground with someone footing it.
Clear leaves and debris first, especially around vents and drainage channels.
Wash with plenty of water and a soft brush; work in sections from front to back.
Check the sealant round every roof fitting as you go (137).
Check the solar panels and their mountings (119).
Check the roof light hinges, seals and that they close fully.
Clear the awning rail channel.
Rinse thoroughly and let it dry before closing anything up.
instructions.afterUse: Note anything found. Do not attempt a repair from a ladder.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Wheel Bolt Torque Check
instructions.description: Checking that the wheels are still done up to the right figure.
instructions.warnings: After any wheel has been removed, re-torque after about 50 km. This is the check that prevents losing a wheel.
instructions.equipment: Torque wrench covering the right range, correct socket, the plated torque figure
steps: Vehicle on level ground, handbrake on, cold.
Find the correct torque figure for your vehicle — it is usually well over 100 Nm on an RV.
Set the torque wrench to that figure.
Work in a star pattern, never round the circle.
Apply smooth pressure until the wrench clicks, once per bolt.
Repeat on every wheel.
Look at each wheel while you are there: no cracks, no missing weights, no oil on the rim.
Reset the torque wrench to zero before storing it.
instructions.afterUse: Note the date. After any tyre work, repeat within 50 km.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Engine Fluids Check
instructions.description: The under-bonnet check before a long trip.
instructions.warnings: Never open the coolant cap on a hot engine. Wait until it is cold enough to hold your hand on the top hose.
instructions.equipment: Correct engine oil, coolant, screenwash, rag
steps: Park level, engine cold, handbrake on.
Engine oil: dipstick out, wipe, back in fully, out again, read. Top up slowly and recheck — overfilling is as bad as underfilling.
Coolant: check between min and max on the expansion tank, cold.
Brake fluid: check the level and note the colour. Dark fluid needs changing.
Screenwash: fill and use a proper additive, not just water.
Power steering if it has a separate reservoir.
Look for any drips, wet patches or crusty residue anywhere in the bay.
Check the belt for cracks and glazing.
instructions.afterUse: Note anything that needed topping up. A fluid that keeps dropping is a leak, not a habit.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Wipers, Washers and Lights
instructions.description: The visibility check — the cheapest safety item on the vehicle.
steps: Wipe the blades with a damp cloth and look for splits, hardening or lifted edges.
Run the wipers on a wet screen and watch for smearing or juddering.
Test both washer jets and aim them if they are off.
Top up screenwash with a proper additive.
Walk round with someone: dipped beam, main beam, sidelights, both indicators, hazards, brake lights, reverse, fog.
Check the number plate light — the one everyone forgets.
Clean all lenses; a dirty lens costs a surprising amount of light.
Check headlight alignment if you have changed the load significantly.
instructions.afterUse: Carry spare bulbs for the common ones, and know where they are.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Step, Door and Lock Lubrication
instructions.where: Entry step, doors, locks, locker catches
instructions.description: Keeping the moving parts moving.
instructions.equipment: Silicone spray, dry PTFE lubricant, graphite or lock lubricant, rag
steps: Clean the step mechanism of grit and road salt first — lubricating over grit makes it worse.
Lubricate the step pivots and runners, then cycle it in and out several times.
Silicone spray on all door and window rubber seals to keep them supple and stop them freezing shut.
Dry lubricant in every lock barrel — not oil, which attracts dirt.
Lubricate all locker catches and hinges.
Check and lubricate the habitation door hinges and the retaining catch.
Wipe off any excess so it does not attract dust.
instructions.notes: Rubber seals treated twice a year last many times longer and stop the door sticking in winter.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Winter Layup — Putting the RV to Bed
instructions.description: Preparing the vehicle for months of standing still.
instructions.warnings: Damp and flat batteries are what ruin vehicles in storage, not cold. Ventilation and charge are the two things that matter.
steps: Drain the entire water system (114).
Clean the inside completely and remove every scrap of food.
Empty, clean and dry the fridge, and leave the door propped open.
Empty and clean the toilet cassette, leave the cap off.
Take out all bedding, cushions and fabrics if you can, or stand them on edge.
Leave locker doors and the wardrobe open.
Place moisture traps through the vehicle.
Batteries: either on a maintenance charger, or removed and stored charged somewhere frost-free.
Tyres: inflate to the upper pressure, and move the vehicle occasionally to avoid flat spots.
Cover the tyres from UV if it is stored outside.
Close all vents against rain but leave the fixed ventilation clear.
Take the gas bottles out if the storage rules require it.
instructions.afterUse: Visit monthly if you can: check for damp, run the engine, move it a metre.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Waking the RV from Storage
instructions.description: Recommissioning after a layup, in the order that finds problems early.
steps: Walk round the outside first, looking for storm damage, and check the roof (139).
Close every drain valve you opened for winterising — check your list from 114.
Refill and sanitise the fresh water system (110).
Run every tap and check for leaks under the sinks and around the water heater.
Reconnect and check the batteries (118).
Reconnect gas, leak-check (122), and light each appliance.
Test the fridge on all three sources (123).
Run the heating (124).
Test every alarm (147) and check the extinguisher date (146).
Tyres: pressures back to running figures and a proper condition check (106).
Engine: fluids (141), start it, let it reach temperature, check for leaks.
Check all documents are in date — insurance, breakdown cover, habitation service.
Take a short local drive before the first real trip.
instructions.afterUse: Anything not right goes on the Actions list immediately — you have time now, and none the week before departure.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Fire Extinguisher and Fire Blanket Check
instructions.description: Making sure the fire kit will work and everyone knows where it is.
instructions.warnings: An extinguisher that is not accessible from the door is not much use. Mounting position matters as much as the extinguisher.
steps: Check the gauge needle is in the green.
Check the pin and tamper seal are intact.
Check the body for dents, rust or corrosion.
Check the service or expiry date.
Turn a dry powder extinguisher upside down and shake it to stop the powder compacting.
Check it is securely in its bracket and can be released one-handed.
Check the fire blanket is in its pouch, unopened, and mounted near but not over the hob.
Make sure everyone on board knows where both are and how to use them.
instructions.afterUse: Note the date. Replace or service according to the manufacturer's interval.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Smoke, Gas and CO Alarm Test
instructions.description: Testing the alarms that only matter on the night they go off.
instructions.warnings: Carbon monoxide has no smell. The alarm is the only thing that will tell you, and only if it works and is in date.
instructions.equipment: Spare batteries
steps: Press and hold the test button on the smoke alarm until it sounds.
Test the CO alarm the same way.
Test the LPG / gas alarm if fitted — these are usually low down, since LPG sinks.
Check the expiry date printed on each unit. Sensors expire, typically 5-10 years, regardless of battery.
Replace batteries at least annually whether or not they are low.
Vacuum dust off the smoke alarm grille.
Check each alarm is mounted where the manufacturer intends — height matters for all three.
Note the test date on the unit with a marker.
instructions.afterUse: If a CO alarm ever sounds: everybody out, doors and windows open, gas off, do not go back in until it has stopped and you know why.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Roadside Breakdown Response
instructions.description: What to do in the first five minutes after stopping unexpectedly.
instructions.warnings: On a motorway the vehicle is the dangerous place, not the safe one. Get out and get behind the barrier.
instructions.equipment: Warning triangle, hi-vis vests for everyone, torch, breakdown policy number
instructions.preparations: Keep the vests within reach of the cab, not in a locker outside.
steps: Get as far left and as far off the carriageway as you can before stopping.
Hazard lights on immediately.
Everyone puts on a hi-vis vest before opening any door.
Everyone out via the doors away from traffic, and behind the barrier or well up the verge.
Warning triangle well back, only if it is safe to walk there — never on a motorway.
Note your exact location: marker post, junction number, or a phone location pin.
Call breakdown assistance with the location, vehicle details, and how many people including any pets.
Stay behind the barrier and wait. Do not attempt repairs on a live carriageway.
instructions.afterUse: Note what happened while it is fresh, for the insurer and for your own maintenance log.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: First Aid Kit Check
instructions.description: Making sure the kit is complete and in date before you need it.
steps: Empty the kit out completely onto a clean surface.
Check every expiry date — sterile dressings, antiseptic, medication all expire.
Replace anything used since last time.
Check the plasters have not gone brittle and the tape still sticks.
Check the contents against a list: dressings, bandages, tape, scissors, tweezers, gloves, antiseptic, burn gel, eye wash, foil blanket, triangular bandage.
Add anything specific to your travel: personal medication, allergy treatment, tick remover, rehydration sachets.
Check you carry the European accident statement form and emergency numbers for the countries you visit.
Repack tidily so things can be found in a hurry, and put it somewhere everyone knows.
instructions.afterUse: Write the check date on the outside of the box.
instructions.notes: 112 is the emergency number across the EU and the UK.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Weekly Apartment Reset
instructions.description: The one session a week that stops everything else piling up.
instructions.equipment: Vacuum, mop, cloths, all-purpose cleaner, bin bags
instructions.preparations: Put music on and set a timer. Doing it fast and imperfectly beats doing it perfectly next month.
steps: Walk through with a basket and put away everything that is not where it lives.
Strip and remake the bed (163).
Start a load of laundry so it runs while you clean (151).
Kitchen: worktops, hob, sink, and the front of the appliances.
Bathroom: quick version — toilet, basin, shower, mirror, floor.
Dust from high to low, all rooms.
Vacuum everywhere, then mop the hard floors.
Bins out and recycling sorted (162).
Water the plants (161).
Finish by clearing the surfaces you look at most — the kitchen worktop and the table.
instructions.notes: Left to itself an apartment does not stay the same, it gets worse. Ninety minutes weekly is far less than the alternative.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Laundry Routine
instructions.description: Washing clothes so they last and actually get dry.
instructions.warnings: Check pockets before anything goes in. A tissue costs you the whole load; a pen costs you the clothes.
steps: Sort by colour and by fabric weight, not just colour — towels with towels, delicates apart.
Check every care label you have not seen before.
Close zips, fasten hooks, turn dark items and printed items inside out.
Do not overload — clothes need room to move or they do not get clean.
Use the right dose of detergent; more is not better and leaves residue.
Choose the lowest effective temperature. 30°C handles most things.
Take the washing out promptly — an hour sitting wet is how it starts to smell.
Shake each item out before hanging; it halves the ironing.
Dry with a window open or the extractor on.
instructions.maintenance: Leave the door and detergent drawer open between washes so the drum dries.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Dishwasher Loading and Care
instructions.description: Loading it so things actually come out clean.
steps: Scrape plates but do not rinse them — modern detergents need something to work on.
Plates on the bottom, facing the centre, not blocking the spray arm.
Bowls and cups on the top, angled down so they do not fill with water.
Nothing overlapping — water has to reach every surface.
Cutlery handles down, except sharp knives.
Keep wood, cast iron, good knives and anything hand-painted out.
Check the spray arms spin freely before closing.
Check the rinse aid and salt levels.
Open the door at the end of the cycle to let the steam out and dry faster.
instructions.maintenance: Clean the filter weekly and run a hot empty cycle with dishwasher cleaner monthly.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Washing Machine Maintenance
instructions.description: Stopping the machine smelling and keeping it working.
instructions.warnings: Turn the water and power off before opening the filter, and have towels down — there will be more water than you expect.
instructions.equipment: Machine cleaner or white vinegar, old towels, shallow tray, cloth
steps: Run a maintenance wash: hottest cycle, empty drum, machine cleaner or 250ml white vinegar.
Pull out the detergent drawer, wash it in hot water, scrub the nozzle behind it.
Wipe the rubber door seal all the way round, folding it back to reach the underside.
Open the filter hatch at the bottom, tray and towels ready, and drain the hose.
Unscrew the filter, clean out the debris, check for coins and hair.
Check the fill and drain hoses for kinks, bulges or damp patches.
Check the machine is level and the feet are firm — most banging is a levelling problem.
Refit everything and run a short rinse cycle to check for leaks.
instructions.afterUse: Leave the door and drawer ajar between washes.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Fridge Clean-Out and Rotation
instructions.description: Weekly clear-out so food gets eaten instead of thrown away.
steps: Take everything out, shelf by shelf, so you never have the whole fridge on the worktop.
Check dates and bin anything gone. Be honest about the jars.
Wipe each shelf and the drawers with warm water and a little bicarbonate — not strong chemicals.
Wipe the door seal; it holds crumbs and mould.
Put things back with the oldest at the front, newest behind.
Keep raw meat on the bottom shelf, always, so it cannot drip onto anything.
Check the temperature is around 4°C — use a fridge thermometer, not the dial.
Note what needs using up this week and plan a meal around it.
instructions.maintenance: Vacuum the condenser coils at the back twice a year — it makes a real difference to running cost.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Oven and Hob Deep Clean
instructions.description: The proper clean, done a few times a year.
instructions.warnings: Ventilate well and wear gloves with any caustic oven cleaner. Keep it away from the door seal and any exposed element.
instructions.equipment: Oven cleaner, bicarbonate of soda, scraper, gloves, cloths
steps: Take the shelves and runners out and soak them in the bath or a large tub with hot water and detergent.
Scrape out loose debris from the oven floor.
Apply oven cleaner, or a bicarbonate paste, and leave it for the stated time — overnight if using paste.
Meanwhile clean the hob: lift the grates, soak them, degrease the surface.
Clean the extractor filters — soak in hot soapy water, or run through the dishwasher if metal.
Wipe the oven out thoroughly, then rinse with clean water several times so nothing is left behind.
Clean the door glass, including between the panes if it comes apart.
Refit everything and run the oven empty at high heat for 20 minutes with the window open.
instructions.afterUse: Wipe spills as they happen and you will only need this twice a year instead of monthly.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Bathroom Deep Clean
instructions.description: Beyond the weekly wipe-round.
instructions.warnings: Never mix bleach with any other cleaner, especially anything containing acid or ammonia. Ventilate throughout.
instructions.equipment: Limescale remover, bathroom cleaner, grout brush, cloths, gloves
steps: Clear everything off every surface first.
Spray limescale remover on taps, shower head and screen, and leave it to work.
Toilet: cleaner under the rim and leave it; then the seat, lid, hinges and the base and pipe behind.
Scrub the grout and the silicone with a stiff brush; treat any mould with a mould spray and leave it on.
Shower screen and tiles, then rinse thoroughly.
Descale the shower head — a bag of vinegar tied over it and left overnight works well.
Basin, then mirror, then the light fitting and extractor grille.
Floor last, edges and behind the toilet included.
Wash the bath mat and the towels.
instructions.afterUse: Squeegee the shower after every use and this stays easy.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Drain Care and Unblocking
instructions.description: Keeping drains flowing and clearing them when they do not.
instructions.warnings: Avoid caustic drain chemicals where you can — they damage pipes and seals over time and are dangerous to have around. Mechanical first.
instructions.equipment: Drain snake or hair tool, plunger, bicarbonate and vinegar, bucket
steps: Monthly prevention: half a cup of bicarbonate followed by a cup of white vinegar, leave 15 minutes, flush with a kettle of hot water.
Never pour cooking fat down a drain — let it set and bin it.
Fit hair traps in the shower and bath and clear them weekly.
For a slow drain, first remove and clean the plug and the visible strainer.
Use a hair-removal tool down the plughole — this clears most bathroom blockages.
If still slow, plunge with the overflow blocked with a wet cloth.
If still blocked, undo the trap under the sink with a bucket underneath and clean it out.
Reassemble, hand-tight, and run water while watching for leaks.
instructions.notes: A smell from a rarely used drain is usually a dry trap. Run the tap for 30 seconds and it goes.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Window Cleaning
instructions.description: Getting glass genuinely clear without streaks.
instructions.warnings: Never lean out of or sit on a window ledge. Anything you cannot reach safely from inside is a job for someone with the right equipment.
instructions.equipment: Squeegee, microfibre cloths, bucket, a little washing-up liquid
instructions.preparations: Choose an overcast day. Sunshine dries the glass before you can finish and that is what causes streaks.
steps: Dust the frames and sills first, or you will just make mud.
Wash the frames and handles before the glass.
Wet the glass with warm water and a couple of drops of washing-up liquid.
Squeegee from the top in overlapping strokes, wiping the blade after each pass.
Finish edges and corners with a dry microfibre cloth.
Buff with a second, completely dry cloth.
Clean the sills and the drainage holes in the bottom of the frame.
Wipe the seals and check for any that are perished.
instructions.notes: Streaks are almost always too much detergent, or direct sun.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Floor Care by Surface
instructions.description: Cleaning each floor type without wrecking it.
instructions.warnings: Wood and laminate hate standing water. Damp mop only, and dry any spill immediately.
steps: Always vacuum or sweep before any wet cleaning — mopping over grit scratches everything.
Sealed wood: barely damp mop with a wood-floor cleaner. No steam, no soaking.
Laminate: same again. Water at the joints is what makes it swell and lift.
Tile: hot water and a neutral cleaner; scrub grout separately as needed.
Vinyl: neutral cleaner only; avoid anything solvent-based.
Carpet: vacuum slowly and in two directions. Speed is what people get wrong.
Blot carpet spills, never rub, and work from the outside inwards.
Put mats at every entrance — most of the dirt in a home walks in.
instructions.maintenance: Felt pads under all furniture legs, checked twice a year.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Dust and Allergen Routine
instructions.description: Reducing dust rather than moving it around.
steps: Always work top down: light fittings, shelf tops, then furniture, then floor.
Use a slightly damp microfibre cloth — a dry duster mostly redistributes.
Do the places nobody does: skirting boards, door frames, radiator fins, behind the TV.
Wash cushion covers and throws monthly.
Wash bedding weekly at 60°C for dust mites (163).
Vacuum mattresses and upholstery monthly.
Keep humidity around 40-50%; both extremes make things worse.
Change or clean any air purifier and extractor filters on schedule.
instructions.notes: Ventilating twice a day for ten minutes with the windows wide does more for air quality than an hour with them tilted.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Houseplant Watering and Care
instructions.description: Keeping plants alive, mostly by watering them less than you think.
instructions.warnings: Far more houseplants die of overwatering than underwatering. When in doubt, wait.
steps: Check each plant individually — push a finger 2-3cm into the soil.
Water only if it is dry at that depth.
Water thoroughly until it runs from the bottom, then empty the saucer after ten minutes.
Never leave a pot standing in water.
Rotate each pot a quarter turn so growth stays even.
Wipe dust off large leaves — it blocks light.
Remove dead leaves and spent flowers.
Feed during the growing season only, roughly fortnightly, and not at all in winter.
Watch for pests on the undersides of leaves.
instructions.afterUse: Before a trip, group plants together away from direct sun and water thoroughly (168).

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Bins and Recycling Sorting
instructions.description: Getting waste out of the flat and sorted correctly.
steps: Check the local collection day and what actually goes in each stream — it varies by area and changes.
Rinse containers before recycling; contamination gets whole loads rejected.
Flatten cardboard and squash bottles to save space.
Keep lids separate if your area requires it.
Glass by colour if your area separates it.
Food waste into the caddy with a compostable liner, emptied often in warm weather.
Batteries, bulbs, electricals and chemicals to the proper collection point — never the general bin.
Wipe the bin and the lid, and put a sheet of newspaper in the bottom.
instructions.notes: A soft plastics bag by the door means the supermarket collection actually gets used.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Bed Linen Change
instructions.description: Changing the bed properly, including the bits usually skipped.
steps: Strip everything off and put it straight in the machine — not on the floor.
While the mattress is bare, vacuum it, especially the seams.
Air the mattress for at least an hour before making it up.
Rotate the mattress head to foot each month, and flip it if it is double-sided.
Wash bedding at 60°C to deal with dust mites.
Fresh fitted sheet, pulled tight at all four corners.
Duvet cover on, shaken out so the filling is even.
Pillowcases, and check the pillows themselves — a pillow older than two years is usually finished.
Air the room with the window wide for ten minutes.
instructions.maintenance: Wash pillows and duvets twice a year if the label allows it.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Home Smoke Alarm Test
instructions.description: Testing the alarms in the apartment.
instructions.warnings: A smoke alarm with the battery taken out because it kept going off is the most dangerous object in a home.
steps: Press and hold the test button on each alarm until it sounds properly.
Check the manufacture or expiry date — sensors expire after around ten years.
Vacuum dust off the cover.
Replace the battery yearly, or sooner at the first chirp.
If it keeps triggering from cooking, move it rather than disabling it.
Check a CO alarm too if you have any gas appliance, boiler or open flue.
Check the escape route is clear and everyone knows it.
Note the test date.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Water Shut-Off and Leak Response
instructions.description: Knowing where the stopcock is before you need it at 2am.
instructions.warnings: Find and test the stopcock today, calmly. A stopcock that has not been turned in ten years will often not turn at all.
instructions.equipment: Towels, bucket, adjustable spanner, tape
instructions.preparations: Locate the main stopcock and the isolating valves for the toilet, basin, sink, washing machine and dishwasher. Photograph them.
steps: If water is escaping: turn off the nearest isolating valve first, or the main stopcock if you cannot find it.
Turn off the electricity at the consumer unit if water is anywhere near sockets, lights or appliances.
Contain what you can with towels and a bucket.
Find the source: appliance hose, tap, toilet, radiator, or from a neighbour above.
Photograph everything for insurance before you clear it up.
If it is coming from above, contact the neighbour and the building management immediately.
Call a plumber or the building emergency number.
Dry thoroughly afterwards and ventilate hard for several days.
instructions.afterUse: Exercise the stopcock a quarter turn twice a year so it does not seize.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Fuse Box and Tripped Breaker
instructions.description: Restoring power safely after a trip, and knowing when not to.
instructions.warnings: If a breaker trips again immediately after resetting, stop. Something is faulty — call an electrician rather than resetting repeatedly.
instructions.preparations: Know where the consumer unit is and keep a torch near it, not inside a cupboard that needs light to open.
steps: Get a torch. Do not use a phone as your only light source.
Open the consumer unit and find the switch that is down or out of line with the others.
Note whether it is a single circuit breaker or the main RCD — an RCD trip means an earth fault somewhere.
Unplug everything on the affected circuit, especially anything recently plugged in.
Reset the breaker firmly to the on position.
Plug appliances back in one at a time, waiting between each, until it trips again — that is your culprit.
If it trips with everything unplugged, it is fixed wiring. Leave it off and call an electrician.
Check whether it is only your flat — if the whole building is out, it is the supply.
instructions.afterUse: Label the consumer unit so next time you know which switch is which.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Heating and Radiator Bleed
instructions.description: Getting the radiators hot all over again.
instructions.warnings: Turn the heating off and let the radiators cool before bleeding, or you will get sprayed with very hot water.
instructions.equipment: Radiator bleed key, cloth, small container
instructions.preparations: Do this at the start of the heating season, before the first cold week rather than during it.
steps: Turn the heating on and let it run, then feel each radiator: cold at the top and warm at the bottom means air.
Turn the heating off and wait for everything to cool.
Start with the radiator lowest and furthest from the boiler.
Hold the container and cloth under the bleed valve at the top corner.
Turn the key slowly anticlockwise, no more than half a turn, until you hear hissing.
As soon as water comes out steadily, close it again.
Work round every radiator, ending with the highest and nearest the boiler.
Check the boiler pressure afterwards — bleeding drops it. Top up to the marked band if needed.
Turn the heating back on and check every radiator heats evenly.
instructions.afterUse: Vacuum behind and underneath the radiators while you are there. Dust there costs real efficiency.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Leaving the Apartment for a Trip
instructions.description: The pre-departure sweep so you can leave without that nagging feeling.
steps: Empty every bin, including the bathroom and the food caddy.
Fridge: eat, freeze or bin anything that will not survive the trip.
Run the dishwasher and empty it; leave it ajar.
Last laundry load done, dried and put away — nothing left damp.
Water the plants thoroughly and group them out of direct sun (161).
Turn off at the socket: TV, chargers, coffee machine, anything with a standby light.
Turn the water off at the stopcock for a longer trip, and isolate the washing machine and dishwasher.
Turn the heating to a frost-protection setting rather than fully off in winter.
Close and lock all windows; check the bathroom one.
Set a light on a timer if you are away a while.
Lock up, and check you have keys, documents, wallet, phone, charger.
instructions.afterUse: Tell a neighbour how long you will be away if it is more than a few days.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Returning Home from a Trip
instructions.description: The first thirty minutes back, done in an order that makes the next day pleasant.
steps: Open every window wide for ten minutes, whatever the weather.
Turn the water back on at the stopcock and run every tap for a minute to flush standing water.
Run the shower hot for a minute for the same reason.
Turn the heating back to its normal setting.
Unpack completely rather than living out of the bag — it takes fifteen minutes now or a week later.
Dirty washing straight into the machine and start it (151).
Check the fridge and bin anything that turned.
Do a shop or an online order for tomorrow morning: milk, bread, coffee.
Check the post and any deliveries.
Put the empty bags away rather than leaving them in the hall.
instructions.notes: Flushing the taps after time away matters — stagnant water in the pipes is worth thirty seconds of running.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Pre-Dive Equipment Check
instructions.description: Checking your own kit before it goes anywhere near the water.
instructions.warnings: These are personal reminders, not training. Dive only within the limits of your certification, your currency and the conditions on the day. If anything here differs from your agency training or the local briefing, follow the training and the briefing. Check your own kit yourself. Never assume it was put away serviceable.
instructions.equipment: BCD, regulator set, cylinder, mask, fins, exposure suit, weights, computer, SMB, cutting tool
steps: Cylinder: check the visual and hydrostatic test dates, and check the contents gauge reads full.
Valve: open and listen, check the O-ring is present and undamaged.
Regulator: check hoses along their whole length for cracks, bulges or corrosion at the crimps.
Breathe from the primary and the alternate — both should be dry and easy.
BCD: inflate fully, leave for a minute, check it holds. Test every dump valve.
Check the low pressure inflator connects, inflates and, crucially, disconnects.
Mask: check the strap and skirt; defog it.
Fins: check the straps and buckles.
Computer: battery level, and the settings for this dive (224).
Cutting tool present and accessible. SMB and reel present.
Weights: correct amount, and check the quick release works.
instructions.afterUse: Anything doubtful gets replaced or the dive gets cancelled. There is always another dive.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Buddy Check
instructions.description: The pre-entry check with your buddy, done properly and out loud.
instructions.warnings: These are personal reminders, not training. Dive only within the limits of your certification, your currency and the conditions on the day. If anything here differs from your agency training or the local briefing, follow the training and the briefing. A buddy check done silently while nodding is not a buddy check. Touch each item and say it.
instructions.preparations: Both fully kitted and ready to enter. This is the last thing before the water.
steps: B — BCD: inflate, deflate, find every dump valve on your buddy, check the inflator works.
W — Weights: confirm the amount, find the release, confirm it is not trapped under anything.
R — Releases: work through every buckle and clip on their kit and know how to undo each one.
A — Air: check the gauge together, both breathe from the primary and the alternate while watching the needle for movement.
F — Final: mask, fins, computer, SMB, cutting tool, camera. Anything hanging is clipped off.
Confirm the dive plan out loud: depth, time, turn pressure, route.
Confirm hand signals, including the ones for this specific dive.
Confirm the lost-buddy procedure and where you surface.
instructions.notes: Whatever mnemonic you learned, the point is the same: two people, out loud, hands on the kit.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Assembling the Scuba Unit
instructions.description: Putting the kit together in the correct order.
instructions.warnings: These are personal reminders, not training. Dive only within the limits of your certification, your currency and the conditions on the day. If anything here differs from your agency training or the local briefing, follow the training and the briefing. Open the cylinder valve slowly. Opening it fast on a modern reg can cause a high-pressure flow that damages the gauge.
steps: Stand the cylinder secure so it cannot fall — that is how ankles and valves get broken.
Check the O-ring in the valve is present and clean.
Slide the BCD onto the cylinder, valve opening facing the same way as the BCD back.
Set the height so the valve is roughly level with the back of your head, then tighten the cam strap on a wet band.
Lift the whole unit by the valve to test the strap holds.
Remove the dust cap from the first stage, check it is dry, and fit it to the valve — DIN screwed in, or yoke seated and hand-tightened.
Route the primary over your right shoulder, alternate on the right, gauges and inflator on the left.
Connect the low pressure inflator to the BCD.
Turn the gauge away from faces, then open the valve slowly, fully, and listen for leaks.
Breathe from both second stages while watching the gauge for needle movement.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Disassembly and Rinsing After the Dive
instructions.description: Breaking the kit down and getting the salt off before it does damage.
instructions.warnings: Never let water into the first stage. The dust cap must be dry and on before anything gets rinsed.
steps: Close the cylinder valve fully.
Purge the second stage to release pressure from the hoses.
Disconnect the low pressure inflator.
Undo the first stage from the valve.
Dry the dust cap thoroughly — blow it dry from the cylinder if you can — and fit it firmly.
Remove the regulator from the cylinder and the BCD from the cylinder.
Rinse the regulator in fresh water without pressing the purge button at any point.
Rinse the BCD inside as well as out: part-fill through the inflator, slosh it, and drain through the dump valve.
Rinse mask, fins, suit, boots, gloves and computer.
Hang everything in the shade to dry — never in direct sun.
Store the BCD partly inflated and the regulator hoses in gentle loops, never tight coils.
instructions.maintenance: Full regulator service at the manufacturer's interval, usually annually or every 100 dives.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Weight Check at the Surface
instructions.description: Finding the right amount of lead for this suit, this water, this cylinder.
instructions.warnings: These are personal reminders, not training. Dive only within the limits of your certification, your currency and the conditions on the day. If anything here differs from your agency training or the local briefing, follow the training and the briefing. Being overweighted is the root of most buoyancy and air-consumption problems, and it makes a controlled ascent harder.
steps: Do this in open water with your buddy, at the start of the dive.
Wear exactly the kit you will dive: same suit, same cylinder, same everything.
Float upright, hold a normal breath, and fully deflate the BCD.
You should float at eye level.
