Keep exhaling through the nose the whole way round — that is what stops water going up it.
Plant both feet on the wall around shoulder width, knees bent about 90 degrees.
Push off on your back or side, in a tight streamline, then rotate to front as you glide.
Hold the streamline for 3-5 metres before the first stroke.
Add 2-3 dolphin kicks in the streamline once the basics are solid.
Practise 10 turns at the end of a session when tired, since that is when they matter.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Open Turn Technique
instructions.description: The turn most people actually use, done efficiently.
steps: Approach the wall at full speed rather than gliding in.
Touch with one hand, keeping the other extended forward.
Tuck the knees up towards the chest as the touching hand pushes off.
Rotate the body sideways as you bring the feet to the wall.
Drop the touching arm back over your head into a streamline.
Plant the feet on the wall and push off hard on your side.
Rotate to front during the glide.
Hold streamline for 2-3 metres before the first stroke.
Practise until it is smooth rather than a stop and start.
instructions.notes: A fast open turn beats a bad tumble turn. Use these in long continuous swims and open water preparation (507).

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Swim Pace Test (CSS)
instructions.description: Measuring your critical swim speed so training paces mean something.
instructions.preparations: Do this fresh, not at the end of a hard week. Same pool, same conditions each time.
steps: Warm up thoroughly, at least 800m including build efforts (501).
Swim 400m as a hard, evenly-paced time trial. Record the time.
Recover fully — 10 minutes of very easy swimming.
Swim 200m as a hard, evenly-paced time trial. Record the time.
Calculate CSS: take (400m time minus 200m time) and divide by 2. That gives your pace per 100m.
Example: 400m in 6:00 (360s) and 200m in 2:50 (170s) gives (360-170)/2 = 95 seconds per 100m.
Use that pace for threshold sets (505).
Cool down 300m easy (502).
Repeat every 6-8 weeks and update your paces.
instructions.afterUse: Record the two times and the calculated pace with the date.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Goggle and Kit Care
instructions.description: Making swim kit last and stop fogging.
instructions.warnings: Never touch the inside of goggle lenses. The anti-fog coating rubs off instantly and never comes back.
steps: Rinse goggles in cool fresh water after every swim — never hot.
Shake the water out; do not wipe the inside.
Dry in the shade, in their case, not left in a wet bag.
If they fog, use a drop of anti-fog solution or a tiny amount of baby shampoo, rinsed lightly.
Rinse the swimsuit or trunks in cold fresh water immediately; chlorine destroys elastane.
Never wring a swimsuit — press the water out.
Dry flat in the shade, never on a radiator or in the sun.
Rinse cap, kickboard, pull buoy and paddles too.
Replace goggles when the seals harden or the strap perishes — usually 6-12 months of regular use.
instructions.notes: Two suits rotated last more than twice as long as one used every day.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Pool Etiquette and Lane Sharing
instructions.description: Sharing a lane without friction.
steps: Look at the lanes before getting in and pick one matching your pace, not your ambition.
Watch a lane for 30 seconds to see the pace and whether they circle or split.
Get in at the shallow end feet first, and wait at the wall for a gap.
Circle swim anticlockwise if there are three or more people.
Keep right if two people are splitting the lane.
Overtake only if there is clear space, tapping the feet ahead first to signal.
If tapped, stop at the next wall and let them past. Do not speed up.
Rest in the corner of the lane, not in the middle of the wall.
Never push off just as someone is coming into the wall.
Shower before getting in — it is not optional and it genuinely helps the water quality.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Post-Swim Skin and Hair Care
instructions.description: Undoing what chlorine does.
steps: Shower as soon as you get out — the longer chlorine sits, the more it does.
Rinse hair thoroughly with fresh water before any shampoo.
Use a swimmer's shampoo or a clarifying one once or twice a week, not every session.
Condition the ends every time.
Wet the hair with fresh water BEFORE swimming next time — hair saturated with clean water absorbs less chlorinated water.
Moisturise the whole body after showering while the skin is still slightly damp.
Dry the ears thoroughly; tilt the head each side. Persistent swimmers' ear is worth seeing someone about.
Rinse and dry all kit before packing it (517).
Rehydrate and eat within 30 minutes.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Cleaning Clubs After a Round
instructions.description: Five minutes that keep the clubs performing and looking cared for.
instructions.warnings: Never soak the heads of woods or any club with a wooden or composite element, and never let water sit at the ferrule where the shaft meets the head.
instructions.equipment: Bucket of warm water, mild washing-up liquid, soft brush, old toothbrush, towels
steps: Fill a bucket with warm — not hot — water and a drop of washing-up liquid.
Stand the irons in it head-down, water no higher than the top of the head, for a few minutes.
Never put the ferrules or shafts in the water.
Brush each groove with a soft brush or old toothbrush, working along the groove not across it.
Clean grooves matter more than anything else here — they are where spin comes from.
Wipe woods and putter with a damp cloth only; do not soak them.
Dry every club thoroughly, especially the hosel area.
Wipe the shafts down, and check for rust or dents while you do.
Wipe the grips with a damp cloth (601).
Check each head for looseness by twisting gently.
instructions.afterUse: Clean the grooves after every few holes too, with a wet towel on the bag.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Grip Care and Regripping Check
instructions.description: Grips are the only contact with the club and the most neglected part of the set.
instructions.warnings: A slick grip makes you hold on tighter, which ruins the swing before it starts. Most people leave grips years past their useful life.
instructions.equipment: Warm soapy water, brush, towel
steps: Wash grips with warm soapy water and a soft brush, then rinse and dry completely.
Do this monthly during the season — it restores much of the tackiness.
Test for wear: the grip should feel tacky, not shiny or hard.
Look for shine on the thumb pad and the lower hand — that is where wear shows first.
Check for cracks, splits and any twisting on the shaft.
Rule of thumb: regrip once a year, or every 40 rounds, whichever comes first.
Note the size — grips that are too small encourage excessive hand action.
If regripping, use the chance to check shaft condition underneath.
instructions.notes: The cheapest meaningful equipment upgrade in golf is a set of fresh grips.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Golf Bag Audit
instructions.description: Turning out the bag so you carry what you need and nothing else.
steps: Empty the bag completely. Everything out onto the floor.
Count the clubs — 14 is the maximum, and carrying 15 is a penalty (619).
Check each club against the list and confirm the set makes sense: no gaps, no duplicates.
Check for grip and groove wear as you go (600, 601).
Balls: keep a dozen of your usual, and separate the scuffed ones for practice.
Tees, markers, pitch repair tool, pencil, scorecard holder.
Glove: check condition and carry a spare (603).
Rangefinder or GPS: check the battery.
Waterproofs, spare towel, umbrella, hat.
Sunscreen, water, food, plasters, painkillers.
Rules book or the app on your phone.
Clean the bag out, including the pockets that collect gravel.
Repack heaviest at the bottom, most-used in the easiest pocket.
instructions.notes: A bag audit is also a weight audit. Most people carry two kilos of things they never use.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Glove and Shoe Care
instructions.description: Making the soft goods last.
instructions.warnings: Never dry a leather glove or leather shoes on a radiator. They harden and crack and are then finished.
steps: Take the glove off between shots and after the round — never leave it in the bag balled up.
Smooth it flat and let it air dry naturally, out of direct heat.
Rotate two gloves — each lasts more than twice as long.
Replace when the palm goes shiny or a seam splits.
Shoes: brush the mud off after every round, including the sole and spikes.
Wipe the uppers with a damp cloth, and use leather conditioner on leather shoes occasionally.
Stuff with newspaper and air dry if they got wet — never near heat.
Check the spikes and replace worn ones; a slipping foot ruins a swing.
Use shoe trees or keep them shaped, and store them out of the bag.
Rotate two pairs if you play often.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Ball Selection and Condition
instructions.description: Choosing a ball and knowing when to bin one.
steps: Pick one model and stick with it. Consistency matters far more than which model.
Match to your game: softer, lower-compression balls for slower swing speeds; urethane covers for more greenside spin.
Play the same ball for a whole round so distances stay consistent.
Note the make, number and any marking so you can identify it — you must be able to identify your ball (615, 616).
Mark every ball distinctively with a pen before the round.
Inspect for cuts, scuffs and out-of-round; a cut ball is a practice ball.
Retire balls that have been in a water hazard for a long time.
Keep balls out of extreme heat — a hot car boot degrades them.
Carry enough: a dozen in the bag, three in the pocket.
instructions.notes: Playing a premium ball you are afraid to lose costs more shots than a cheaper one you swing freely at.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Range Warm-Up Routine
instructions.description: Warming up before a round, in the right order.
instructions.warnings: A warm-up is not a practice session. Do not start rebuilding your swing on the range twenty minutes before you tee off.
steps: Start with the body, not a club: arm circles, trunk rotations, leg swings, 5 minutes.
Hold a club across the shoulders and rotate gently, 10 each way.
Start hitting with a wedge, half swings, 10 balls.
Move to a short iron, three-quarter swings, 10 balls.
Mid iron, full swings, 10 balls.
Hybrid or fairway wood, 5 balls.
Driver, 5-8 balls only.
Finish with the club you will hit off the first tee, 3 balls, with a full pre-shot routine (606).
Then the putting green: long lag putts first for pace, 10 minutes.
Finish with 10 short putts holed, to leave with a good feeling.
Arrive at the tee 5 minutes early, not 30 seconds late.
instructions.notes: Play the last few range balls as if they were shots on the course, with the full routine. That is the bridge.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Pre-Shot Routine
instructions.description: The same sequence before every shot, which is what makes it repeatable under pressure.
instructions.warnings: The routine must be the same length every time. A routine that gets longer under pressure is not a routine.
steps: Behind the ball: assess lie, distance, wind, slope and trouble.
Pick a specific target — a branch, not "the fairway".
Choose the club and commit to it. Doubt is what produces the bad swing.
Pick an intermediate target on the ground a foot or two in front of the ball on the target line.
One practice swing that rehearses the actual shot, not a generic swing.
Step in, set the clubface to the intermediate target first.
Then build the stance around the clubface, not the other way round.
One look at the target, one waggle, and go.
Whole thing under 20 seconds. Same every time.
If anything interrupts it, step away and start again from the beginning.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Putting Drill — Gate Drill
instructions.description: Training a square face and a centred strike.
instructions.equipment: Two tees, putter, several balls
steps: Find a flat straight putt of about 1 metre.
Push two tees into the green just wider than the putter head, forming a gate the putter must swing through.
Make 10 putts, keeping the putter clear of both tees.
If you clip a tee, note which one — the outside tee means an out-to-in path, the inside means in-to-out.
Narrow the gate as you improve.
Second gate: two tees just wider than the ball, about 30cm ahead on the target line.
The ball must start through both gates — this trains face angle at impact.
Make 20 putts through both gates.
Move to 2 metres and repeat.
Finish by holing 10 in a row from 1 metre; start again if you miss.
instructions.notes: Face angle at impact accounts for the vast majority of a putt's starting direction. This drill trains exactly that.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Putting Drill — Distance Ladder
instructions.description: Training pace, which is what actually costs three-putts.
instructions.warnings: Three-putts come from bad pace far more than bad line. This is the more valuable putting drill.
steps: Place tees or markers at 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 metres from a starting point.
Putt one ball to each marker in turn, trying to stop it within a putter-length.
Do not aim at a hole — aim at the distance.
Go up the ladder, then back down it.
Note how the stroke length changes; keep the tempo identical and change only the length.
Second version: putt to the fringe and try to just reach it without going over.
Third version: with eyes closed, putt and then guess whether it was short or long before looking. This builds real feel.
Finish with 10 lag putts from random long distances, counting how many finish inside a 1-metre circle.
instructions.notes: Aim to leave every long putt inside the circle you can hole out from. That is the whole skill.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Chipping Drill — Landing Spot
instructions.description: Learning to control where the ball lands rather than where it finishes.
instructions.equipment: Towel or hoop, several clubs, balls
steps: Put a towel or hoop down as a landing target about 2 metres onto the green.
Chip 10 balls with a sand wedge, trying to land each on the towel and ignoring where it finishes.
Now hit the same shot with a pitching wedge, same landing spot — watch how much further it runs.
Repeat with a 9 iron, then an 8, then a 7.
Learn your ratios: how much carry versus roll each club gives from that lie.
Write the ratios down. Roughly, sand wedge 1:1, pitching wedge 1:2, 8 iron 1:4, 7 iron 1:5.
Now play the game backwards: pick a hole, choose the landing spot first, then the club that makes it work.
Set up with weight slightly forward, hands ahead, and keep the lower body quiet.
Finish with 10 chips to a real hole, counting how many finish inside a metre.
instructions.notes: Amateurs choose a club and hope. Good players choose a landing spot and then the club.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Bunker Drill
instructions.description: Getting out first time, every time.
instructions.warnings: In a bunker in play, do not ground the club before the stroke and do not touch the sand on the backswing — see 614 for what you may and may not do.
steps: Draw a line in the sand and practise swinging so the club enters on the line, without a ball.
Do 10 swings, checking each divot starts on the line.
Now place a ball 5cm behind the line and hit the sand, not the ball.
Set-up: open the clubface FIRST, then take your grip. Not the other way round.
Feet dug in for stability, weight slightly forward, ball forward in the stance.
Open the stance and swing along your body line, not at the target.
Commit to accelerating through — the sand slows the club, so a decelerating swing leaves it in.
Take a divot of sand roughly the size of a banknote.
Hit 20 shots aiming to get every one out, not close.
Then practise from a plugged lie: square face, steeper swing, expect more run.
Rake the bunker properly before you leave.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Structured Range Practice Plan
instructions.description: Practising properly instead of hitting a bucket of balls.
instructions.warnings: Hitting the same club repeatedly from the same lie is the least transferable practice there is. It feels productive and mostly is not.
steps: Decide the purpose before you start: technique, or transfer to the course. Not both.
Warm up properly first, 10 minutes (605).
Block practice, 20 balls: one club, one change, slow and deliberate. This is for technique.
Rest and reset.
Random practice, 40 balls: change club and target every single ball.
Play nine imaginary holes: choose a shot, pick a club, full routine, one ball, then move on (606).
Score yourself: did the shot achieve what you intended, yes or no.
Include the awkward shots you avoid: half wedges, punch shots, into wind.
Finish with 10 balls to a specific target with a full routine each time.
Note what you worked on and what you will work on next time.
instructions.notes: Random practice feels worse and transfers far better. That trade is the whole point.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Alignment Drill
instructions.description: Checking that where you aim is where you are actually aimed.
instructions.warnings: Almost everyone aims right of where they think, then compensates in the swing. Check it with sticks, not with feel.
instructions.equipment: Two alignment sticks or clubs
instructions.preparations: Check whether alignment sticks are permitted at your range before laying them out.
steps: Pick a specific target.
Lay one stick on the ground pointing at the target, just outside the ball.
Lay the second parallel to it, along your toe line.
Set up and look down: your feet, knees, hips and shoulders should all match the toe-line stick.
Now look at the target from the stance. It will probably feel like you are aimed left. That feeling is the point.
Hit 10 balls with the sticks down.
Take the sticks away and set up again by feel, then lay a club along your toes and check.
Repeat until your feel matches reality.
Check the clubface too — set the face to the target first, then build the stance (606).

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Tempo Drill
instructions.description: Training a consistent rhythm, which does more for contact than any position.
steps: Count a rhythm out loud: "one-two-three" back, "one" down. The ratio matters more than the speed.
Hit 10 balls counting out loud. It feels ridiculous and it works.
Feet-together drill: 10 balls with your feet touching. This forces a smooth, balanced swing.
One-handed swings: 10 with the lead arm only, half swing, for control.
Hit 10 balls at 70% effort and note the distance — usually barely shorter, and much straighter.
Swing with your eyes closed for 5 balls and feel the balance.
Hold the finish position for three full seconds on every shot. If you cannot, you swung too hard.
Practise with a heavy club or a weighted trainer to feel the sequence.
instructions.notes: If you can hold a balanced finish, the tempo was right. It is the simplest self-check in golf.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Rules — Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
instructions.description: Free relief from ground under repair, immovable obstructions, animal holes and temporary water.
instructions.warnings: Rules summarised in plain language for on-course recall. The Rules of Golf are the authority — check the official rule or ask the committee if anything is unclear or if money or a competition depends on it.
steps: Abnormal course conditions are: temporary water, ground under repair, animal holes, and immovable obstructions such as paths, sprinkler heads and staked areas.
You get free relief if the condition interferes with your lie, your stance, or your intended swing.
It does NOT include interference with your line of play, except on the putting green.
Find the nearest point of complete relief — nearest, not nicest, and no closer to the hole.
Mark that point.
Drop within one club-length of it, no closer to the hole, in the same area of the course.
Drop from knee height.
The ball must come to rest in the relief area; if it rolls out, re-drop, and if it rolls out again, place it.
In a bunker, free relief must be taken within the bunker; or you may take it outside for one penalty stroke.
On the putting green you may place the ball at the nearest point of complete relief.
instructions.notes: "Nearest point of complete relief" is the phrase people get wrong. It may well be in a worse spot than where you were.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Rules — Penalty Areas
instructions.description: What to do when the ball is in the red or yellow stakes.
instructions.warnings: Rules summarised in plain language for on-course recall. The Rules of Golf are the authority — check the official rule or ask the committee if anything is unclear or if money or a competition depends on it.
steps: Penalty areas are marked yellow or red. Any water, and anything else the committee has marked.
You may play the ball as it lies from a penalty area with no penalty, and you may ground your club and move loose impediments.
If you take relief, it is one penalty stroke.
Yellow penalty area, two options: play again from where you last played; or drop back on the line from the hole through the point where the ball last crossed the edge, going back as far as you like.
Red penalty area, three options: both of the above, plus lateral relief.
Lateral relief: drop within two club-lengths of where the ball last crossed the edge, no closer to the hole.
Establish where the ball LAST CROSSED the edge, not where it ended up. This is the point that matters.
If it is known or virtually certain the ball is in the penalty area, you may take relief without finding it.
If that is not certain, the ball is lost and you must play again from the previous spot with a stroke-and-distance penalty.
Drop from knee height in all cases.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Rules — Unplayable Ball
instructions.description: Your options when the ball is findable but not hittable.
instructions.warnings: Rules summarised in plain language for on-course recall. The Rules of Golf are the authority — check the official rule or ask the committee if anything is unclear or if money or a competition depends on it.
steps: You alone decide the ball is unplayable, anywhere on the course except in a penalty area.
It always costs one penalty stroke.
Option 1 — stroke and distance: play again from where you last played.
Option 2 — back-on-the-line: keep the spot of the ball between you and the hole, and drop anywhere on that line, as far back as you like.
Option 3 — lateral: drop within two club-lengths of the ball, no closer to the hole.
In a bunker, all three options are available but options 2 and 3 must keep the ball in the bunker.
In a bunker you may alternatively drop outside on the back-on-the-line option for a total of two penalty strokes.
Drop from knee height into the correct relief area.
If it lands and rolls out of the relief area twice, place it where it second touched the ground.
Think before you declare: sometimes the stroke-and-distance option is better than a bad lie two club-lengths away.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Rules — Provisional Ball
instructions.description: Saving a walk back when the ball might be lost or out of bounds.
instructions.warnings: Rules summarised in plain language for on-course recall. The Rules of Golf are the authority — check the official rule or ask the committee if anything is unclear or if money or a competition depends on it.
steps: Play a provisional when the ball may be out of bounds or lost anywhere OTHER than a penalty area.
You must announce it clearly before playing: say the word "provisional". Saying "I'll hit another" is not enough and makes the new ball in play.
Play the provisional from the same spot as the original.
You may keep playing the provisional as you walk forward, as long as it stays further from the hole than where the original is likely to be.
If you find the original in bounds within three minutes, you must play it and abandon the provisional.
If the original is not found in three minutes, or is out of bounds, the provisional is in play under stroke and distance.
The three minutes starts when you or your caddie begin searching.
If the original turns out to be in a penalty area, you may not use the provisional — take penalty area relief instead (615).
Use a visibly different ball or marking so you can tell them apart (604).
instructions.notes: Announcing it properly is the bit people get wrong, and it costs strokes.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Rules — On the Putting Green
instructions.description: The things you may and may not do once you are on the green.
instructions.warnings: Rules summarised in plain language for on-course recall. The Rules of Golf are the authority — check the official rule or ask the committee if anything is unclear or if money or a competition depends on it.
steps: You may mark, lift and clean your ball on the green at any time. Mark it first, always.
Mark directly behind the ball with a coin or marker before lifting.
You may repair almost any damage on the green: pitch marks, shoe damage, old holes, animal damage.
You may NOT repair natural imperfections, aeration holes, or normal wear of the hole.
You may touch your line of play, but you may not improve it by pressing anything down.
The flagstick may be left in or taken out — your choice, no penalty either way.
If your ball hits an unattended flagstick left in the hole, there is no penalty.
No penalty if your ball accidentally moves on the green — replace it on the original spot.
If wind moves your ball after you replaced it, play it from the new spot; if you had not yet replaced it, replace it.
Repair your pitch mark before you leave, and one other.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Scoring and Handicap Recording
instructions.description: Keeping the card correctly and submitting it.
instructions.warnings: In stroke play, signing for a lower score than you took disqualifies you. Signing for a higher one stands. Check the card carefully.
steps: Before starting, confirm the maximum of 14 clubs in the bag (602).
Exchange cards with your marker and confirm each other's name and handicap.
Record your playing partner's gross score hole by hole; they record yours.
Check with each other at the end of each hole, not at the end of the round.
Record the hole score only — the marker is not responsible for the handicap arithmetic.
Note any penalty strokes as they happen, while you remember why.
If unsure of a ruling, play two balls in stroke play and get it settled before signing (Rule 20.1c).
At the end: check every hole score, then the total.
Both you and your marker sign the card.
Submit before leaving the clubhouse, within the time the committee requires.
For handicap purposes, record every qualifying round, including the bad ones.
instructions.notes: Recording only your good rounds gives you a handicap you cannot play to. Submit them all.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Breath-Focus Meditation
instructions.description: The foundational practice — attention on the breath, returning when it wanders.
instructions.preparations: Set a timer so you are not checking the clock. Phone on do not disturb.
steps: Sit upright but not rigid — chair or cushion, both fine. Feet flat or legs crossed.
Hands resting wherever they are comfortable. Eyes closed, or softly open looking down.
Take three deliberate breaths to settle, then let the breath find its own rhythm.
Rest attention where the breath is most obvious: the nostrils, the chest, or the belly. Pick one and stay.
Do not control the breath. Watch it.
When you notice the mind has wandered, that noticing IS the practice. Gently return.
It will wander constantly. That is not failure, that is the exercise repeating.
No judgement about how many times. A hundred returns is a hundred repetitions.
When the timer sounds, sit for a moment before moving.
instructions.afterUse: Note only whether you sat, not how it went. The streak matters more than the quality.
instructions.notes: Start at 5 minutes daily rather than 30 minutes weekly. Consistency is the whole thing.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Body Scan
instructions.description: Moving attention slowly through the body, part by part.
steps: Lie on your back, arms at your sides, or sit comfortably.
Take a few slow breaths and let the body settle into the surface beneath it.
Bring attention to the toes of the left foot. Notice whatever is there — warmth, pressure, tingling, or nothing at all.
"Nothing at all" is a perfectly valid observation. Do not manufacture a sensation.
Move slowly upward: foot, ankle, calf, knee, thigh.
Repeat on the right leg.
Then pelvis, lower back, abdomen, chest, upper back.
Then left hand and arm, right hand and arm.
Then shoulders, neck, jaw, face, scalp.
Finish by holding a sense of the whole body at once for a minute or two.
If you fall asleep doing this at night, that is a feature not a failure.
instructions.notes: Excellent for winding down at the end of a day, and for noticing tension you had stopped registering.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Loving-Kindness (Metta)
instructions.description: Deliberately cultivating goodwill, starting with yourself.
steps: Sit comfortably and take a few settling breaths.
Bring to mind a feeling of warmth — the memory of someone or something you feel simply fond of.
Direct it at yourself first, silently repeating phrases: may I be safe, may I be well, may I be at ease.
Repeat slowly. Feel it if you can; say it anyway if you cannot.
Now bring to mind someone you love easily. Same phrases: may you be safe, may you be well, may you be at ease.
Now a neutral person — someone you see but barely know.
Now someone you find difficult. Start with mildly difficult, not the hardest person in your life.
Finally, widen it outwards: everyone in this building, this town, everywhere.
Sit for a moment without phrases before finishing.
instructions.notes: Starting with yourself is the part people skip and the part that matters most.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Noting Practice
instructions.description: Labelling experience lightly as it arises.
steps: Sit and settle with a few breaths.
Rest in open attention rather than on one object.
When something takes your attention, note it with a single quiet word: "thinking", "hearing", "feeling", "planning", "remembering".
Say the word gently in the mind — a whisper, not an announcement.
Then let it go and return to open attention.
Do not analyse the content. "Thinking" is enough; you do not need to know what about.
If notes come thick and fast, slow down and note less often.
Notice the pattern over the session: what turns up most? Planning? Judging? That is useful information.
Finish by dropping the noting and just sitting for the last minute.
instructions.notes: Very good for people who find pure breath focus frustrating — it gives the analytical mind a job.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Walking Meditation
instructions.where: A quiet path 10-20 paces long, or outdoors
instructions.description: The same practice, moving.
steps: Find a stretch you can walk back and forth along without navigating.
Stand still for a moment and feel the feet on the ground.
Walk slower than normal — deliberately, but not theatrically slowly.
Put attention on the sensation of the feet: lifting, moving, placing.
You can note it: "lifting, moving, placing".
At the end of the stretch, stop, pause, turn deliberately, and pause again before setting off.
When the mind wanders, return to the feet — same as returning to the breath.
Keep the gaze soft and a few metres ahead, not on your feet.
Outdoors, widen occasionally to include sounds and air on the skin, then return to the feet.
instructions.notes: Good on a day when sitting still feels impossible, and easy to do beside the RV on a campsite.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Box Breathing
instructions.description: A short, structured breathing pattern for settling the nervous system quickly.
instructions.warnings: If you feel dizzy or light-headed, stop and breathe normally. Never do breath-holds in or near water.
steps: Sit upright with the feet flat on the floor.
Exhale fully to empty.
Inhale through the nose for a count of 4.
Hold for a count of 4.
Exhale through the nose for a count of 4.
Hold empty for a count of 4.
That is one round. Repeat for 8-10 rounds.
Keep the count comfortable — reduce to 3 if 4 feels strained.
Finish by letting the breath return to normal and noticing the difference.
instructions.notes: Five minutes of this before a difficult conversation, a race start, or a night you cannot sleep.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Evening Wind-Down Meditation
instructions.description: A practice designed to help you stop, not to help you focus.
steps: Do this in bed or in a chair in low light, screens already off.
Start with three long slow exhales — longer out than in.
Set the pattern: in for 4, out for 6-8. The long exhale is what does the work.
Let go of counting after a few minutes and let the breath be slow and natural.
Do a quick body scan from head to toes, releasing the jaw, the shoulders, the hands (701).
Mentally set the day down: acknowledge one thing that went well and one thing you are letting go of until tomorrow.
If a to-do surfaces, note it on paper beside the bed rather than trying to remember it.
Rest attention on the weight of the body on the mattress.
No timer. Falling asleep is an acceptable outcome.

revisionHistory.changes: Created — imported from the starter library

instructions.title: Morning Sit
instructions.description: A short practice at the start of the day, before anything else gets in.
instructions.warnings: The main obstacle is the phone. Do not look at it before you sit — once you have, the sit is a different and much harder thing.
steps: Sit before you check anything. Ideally before coffee, definitely before the phone.
Same place, same time, same seat. Remove every decision from it.
Set a timer for 10 minutes.
Three deliberate breaths to arrive.
Then breath focus (700), or noting (703) — pick one and stay with it.
If the mind is very busy, count breaths 1 to 10 and start again.
When the timer sounds, sit for another 20 seconds before standing.
Before opening the phone, take a moment to decide what actually matters today.
instructions.notes: Ten minutes every morning beats an hour on Sunday. Anchor it to something you already do without fail.

instructions.title: Open Awareness
instructions.description: Resting in awareness itself rather than on a chosen object.
instructions.preparations: Easier after some breath practice. Start with 5 minutes of breath focus, then open out.
steps: Sit and settle with 5 minutes of breath focus (700).
Then deliberately let go of the breath as an object.
Let attention be wide and receptive — like listening to a whole room rather than one voice.
Whatever arises — sound, sensation, thought — let it arise and pass without following it.
Do not push anything away and do not chase anything.
If you get lost in a train of thought, come back to the breath for a few breaths, then open out again.
Notice that awareness itself is not disturbed by what appears in it.
Sit for the last minutes without any technique at all.
instructions.notes: This is harder than it sounds and easier than it seems. Do not worry about doing it right.

instructions.title: Three-Minute Breathing Space
instructions.description: A short reset that fits into any day, anywhere.
steps: Stop whatever you are doing. Sit or stand upright.
Minute one — WIDE: what is here right now? Notice thoughts, feelings and body sensations without fixing anything. Just acknowledge.
Minute two — NARROW: bring attention fully to the breath. Follow a few breaths all the way in and all the way out.
Minute three — WIDE AGAIN: expand attention to the whole body, posture, the face, the space around you.
Then carry on with your day.
Use it between tasks, before a meal, in a traffic queue, or when you notice tension.
Three minutes is enough. Do not extend it into a full sit — the brevity is what makes it usable.
instructions.notes: The most practically useful practice on this list, because it actually fits into real days.

instructions.title: Full-Body Morning Mobility Flow
instructions.description: Ten minutes to move everything before the day starts.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Morning tissue is stiffer — move gently and do not force range first thing.
steps: Cat-cow on hands and knees, 10 slow rounds, breathing with the movement.
Child's pose with side reaches, 30 seconds each side.
Thread the needle, 8 each side, for the thoracic spine.
Downward dog with alternating heel presses, 30 seconds.
World's greatest stretch, 5 each side — lunge, elbow to instep, rotate open.
Hip circles on hands and knees, 8 each direction each leg.
Deep squat hold, 60 seconds, holding something for support if needed.
Standing forward fold with soft knees, 30 seconds.
Shoulder rolls and neck circles, 5 each direction.
Finish standing tall with 5 deep breaths.
instructions.notes: The point is to move everything a little, not to stretch anything a lot.

instructions.title: Hip Opener Sequence
instructions.description: Targeted hip work for people who sit and cycle.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Hips respond to time, not force. Long gentle holds beat hard short ones.
steps: 90/90 sitting: both knees at 90 degrees, front and back leg, sit tall. Hold 60 seconds each side.
90/90 transitions: rotate the knees side to side without using the hands, 10 slow reps.
Pigeon pose, 90 seconds each side, chest down if comfortable.
Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch: squeeze the back glute, tuck the pelvis, 60 seconds each side.
Add a slight side bend away from the back leg to reach the psoas.
Frog stretch, knees wide, 60-90 seconds, rocking gently.
Butterfly sitting, feet together, 60 seconds, gentle pressure on the knees.
Deep squat hold, 90 seconds, working the elbows inside the knees.
Lying figure-four, 60 seconds each side.
instructions.afterUse: Best done after activity or a warm shower, when the tissue is warm.

instructions.title: Thoracic Spine Mobility
instructions.description: Restoring rotation and extension in the mid-back.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Keep the movement in the mid-back. If you feel it in the low back, you are arching rather than extending the thoracic spine.
instructions.equipment: Foam roller optional
steps: Foam roller extensions: roller across the mid-back, hands supporting the head, extend gently over it. 10 reps, moving the roller up one segment at a time.
Do not let the ribs flare — keep the core lightly engaged.
Open book: lie on your side, knees bent at 90, arms out in front. Rotate the top arm open and follow it with your eyes. 10 each side, slow.
Thread the needle from hands and knees, 10 each side.
Quadruped thoracic rotation: hand behind head, rotate the elbow up and open, 10 each side.
Seated rotation: sit tall, arms crossed on the chest, rotate slowly, 10 each side.
Wall angels: back flat to the wall, arms up and down keeping contact, 10 slow reps.
Prayer stretch: forearms on a chair, sink the chest down, 60 seconds.
instructions.notes: The mid-back stiffens from sitting and cycling. When it will not rotate, the low back and the shoulders do the job instead.

instructions.title: Shoulder Mobility
instructions.description: Keeping the shoulders moving freely and safely.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Shoulders do not respond well to being forced. Small ranges, controlled, repeated.
instructions.equipment: Band, broomstick or towel
steps: Arm circles, 15 each direction, small building to large.
Band or stick pass-throughs: wide grip, take the arms overhead and behind, 10 slow reps. Widen the grip if it pinches.
Wall slides: back and arms to the wall, slide up and down keeping contact, 10 reps.
Band pull-aparts, 15 reps, squeezing the shoulder blades.
External rotation with a band, elbow at the side, 15 each arm.
Doorway pec stretch at three heights — low, middle, high — 30 seconds each.
Sleeper stretch for internal rotation, 30 seconds each side, gently.
Scapular push-ups from a plank, 10 reps.
Prone Y-T-W raises, 8 each position.
instructions.notes: Essential for swimmers and for anyone who spends the day at a desk.

instructions.title: Ankle Mobility
instructions.description: The joint everyone ignores until the knee starts complaining.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting.
steps: Knee-to-wall test: foot 10cm from a wall, drive the knee forward over the toes without lifting the heel. Note the distance you can achieve.
Do 10 reps each side, then measure again.
Repeat at increasing distances from the wall to find your limit.
Calf stretch straight-leg against a wall, 45 seconds each side.
Calf stretch bent-knee for the soleus, 45 seconds each side.
Ankle circles, 15 each direction each foot.
Heel walks and toe walks, 20 steps of each.
Kneeling toe stretch: sit back on tucked toes, 30-60 seconds.
Single-leg balance, 30 seconds each side, then again with eyes closed.
instructions.afterUse: Note the knee-to-wall distance monthly. It is a real, measurable number that responds to work.

instructions.title: Hamstring and Posterior Chain Stretch
instructions.description: The back of the body, which shortens from sitting and running.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Never bounce into a hamstring stretch. If you feel nerve-like symptoms down the leg rather than muscular stretch, back off.
steps: Warm up first — 5 minutes of walking or easy movement. Never stretch cold hamstrings.
Standing forward fold with soft knees, 60 seconds, letting the head hang heavy.
Single-leg forward fold, 45 seconds each side, hips square.
Supine hamstring stretch with a strap or towel, 60 seconds each side, other leg flat.
Add gentle ankle pumps during the hold to include the calf.
Seated straddle, 60 seconds centre, 45 seconds each side.
Glute bridge, 15 reps, for active work rather than stretch.
Good mornings with a broomstick, 15 reps, hinging at the hips.
Nerve glides: lying with the leg raised, flex and point the foot 10 times, gently.
instructions.afterUse: Best after a run or a warm shower, never before.

instructions.title: Desk-Break Mobility
instructions.description: Five minutes to undo an hour of sitting.
instructions.warnings: The best posture is the next one. No sitting position is good enough to hold for three hours.
steps: Stand up. That alone is most of the benefit.
Neck: chin tucks, 10 reps. Then ear to shoulder, 20 seconds each side.
Shoulder rolls, 10 backwards.
Doorway pec stretch, 30 seconds.
Standing thoracic rotation, 10 each side (802).
Hip flexor stretch in a standing lunge, 30 seconds each side.
Standing forward fold, 30 seconds.
10 bodyweight squats.
Look at something at least 20 metres away for 20 seconds — the eyes need the break too.
Set a reminder for every 45-60 minutes.

instructions.title: Post-Run Stretch Routine
instructions.description: The specific stretches that matter after running.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Do this while still warm, within about 15 minutes of finishing.
steps: Walk for 3 minutes first and let the heart rate come down (302).
Calves, straight leg against a wall, 45 seconds each side.
Calves, bent knee for the soleus, 45 seconds each side.
Standing quad stretch, 45 seconds each side, knees together, pelvis tucked.
Half-kneeling hip flexor, 60 seconds each side. This is the most important one for runners.
Hamstring stretch, standing or supine with a strap, 45 seconds each side.
Figure-four glute stretch, 60 seconds each side.
Standing IT band stretch, crossing one leg behind, 45 seconds each side.
Piriformis stretch seated, 45 seconds each side.
Finish with a 30-second standing forward fold.
instructions.notes: The hip flexors are the runner's chronic problem and the stretch most often skipped.

instructions.title: Foam Rolling Routine
instructions.description: Self-massage for tight tissue, done in a way that helps.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Roll muscle, never bone or joint. Avoid rolling directly on the IT band itself or the lower back — work the glutes and TFL instead.
instructions.equipment: Foam roller, massage ball
steps: Roll slowly — about 2-3cm per second. Fast rolling does nothing.
When you find a tender spot, stop on it and breathe for 20-30 seconds until it eases.
Calves: 60 seconds each, rotating the leg in and out.
Quads: 60 seconds each, one leg at a time.
Adductors: 45 seconds each, roller under the inner thigh.
Glutes: sit on the roller, ankle on the opposite knee, 60 seconds each side.
TFL and outer hip: 45 seconds each side.
Upper back: roller across, hands behind head, 60 seconds (802).
Lats: on your side, arm overhead, 45 seconds each.
Feet: massage ball underfoot, 60 seconds each.
instructions.notes: Pain during rolling should be a "good" ache, around 6 or 7 out of 10. Grimacing and holding your breath is too hard.

instructions.title: Evening Relaxation Stretch
instructions.description: Slow, passive stretching to wind down before sleep.
steps: Dim the lights and put the phone away first.
Child's pose, 2 minutes, breathing slowly.
Supine twist, 90 seconds each side, letting the knees fall and the shoulders stay down.
Happy baby, 90 seconds.
Reclined butterfly, feet together, 2 minutes.
Legs up the wall, 3-5 minutes. Excellent after a day on your feet or a long run.
Supine hamstring with a strap, 60 seconds each side, gently.
Lying on the back, knees to chest, gentle rocking, 60 seconds.
Finish flat on your back for 2 minutes with slow long exhales (706).
Move straight to bed rather than back to a screen.
instructions.notes: This is not a flexibility session. Hold everything easily and let the breath be long.

instructions.title: Full-Body Strength Session A
instructions.description: A balanced whole-body session built round a squat and a press.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Form before load, always. If the technique changes, the set is over regardless of the number on the bar.
instructions.equipment: Barbell or dumbbells, bench, rack
instructions.preparations: Warm up first (909).
steps: Warm up thoroughly, including 2 light sets of the first exercise (909).
Back squat or goblet squat: 4 sets of 6-8. Depth to at least parallel, knees tracking over toes, chest up.
Bench press or dumbbell press: 4 sets of 6-8. Shoulder blades retracted, feet planted.
Romanian deadlift: 3 sets of 8-10. Hinge at the hips, bar close, back flat, feel it in the hamstrings.
Bent-over row: 3 sets of 8-10. Flat back, pull to the lower ribs.
Overhead press: 3 sets of 8-10. Ribs down, glutes squeezed, do not arch the low back.
Plank: 3 x 45 seconds, straight line from head to heels.
Rest 2-3 minutes between compound sets, 90 seconds for the rest.
Log the weights and reps every session.
instructions.afterUse: Stretch briefly and eat protein within the hour.

instructions.title: Full-Body Strength Session B
instructions.description: The complementary session — deadlift and pull focused.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. The deadlift is the exercise where ego costs most. Start light and earn the weight.
steps: Warm up thoroughly (909).
Deadlift: 4 sets of 5. Bar over mid-foot, flat back, push the floor away, lock out with the glutes.
Reset every rep rather than bouncing off the floor.
Front squat or split squat: 3 sets of 8 each side.
Pull-up or lat pulldown: 4 sets of 6-10.
Dumbbell incline press: 3 sets of 8-10.
Walking lunges: 3 sets of 10 each leg.
Face pulls: 3 sets of 15, for the rear shoulder and posture.
Hanging knee raise or dead bug: 3 sets of 12.
Rest 2-3 minutes after deadlifts and squats.
instructions.afterUse: Expect the deadlift to cost more recovery than anything else. Do not schedule a hard run the next day.

instructions.title: Lower Body Strength
instructions.description: A dedicated leg session.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting.
steps: Warm up including 10 minutes of easy cycling and dynamic drills (909).
Back squat: 4 sets of 5-8.
Romanian deadlift: 4 sets of 8.
Bulgarian split squat: 3 sets of 8-10 each leg. Brutal and worth it.
Leg press or hack squat: 3 sets of 10-12.
Standing calf raise: 4 sets of 12-15, full range, pausing at the top and bottom.
Seated calf raise: 3 sets of 15, for the soleus.
Nordic curl or hamstring curl: 3 sets of 8.
Single-leg glute bridge: 3 sets of 12 each side.
Finish with hip mobility (801).

instructions.title: Upper Body Push
instructions.description: Chest, shoulders and triceps.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Shoulder pain on pressing is a signal to change the movement, not to push through it.
steps: Warm up including shoulder mobility and band work (909, 803).
Bench press or dumbbell bench: 4 sets of 6-8.
Overhead press: 4 sets of 6-8.
Incline dumbbell press: 3 sets of 8-10.
Dips or close-grip press: 3 sets of 8-10.
Lateral raises: 3 sets of 12-15, light and controlled.
Cable or dumbbell fly: 3 sets of 12.
Tricep pushdown or overhead extension: 3 sets of 12.
Finish with 2 sets of 15 band pull-aparts to balance the pressing volume.
Stretch the chest and front shoulder afterwards (803).

instructions.title: Upper Body Pull
instructions.description: Back and biceps — the half most people undertrain.
steps: Warm up including band pull-aparts and scapular work (909).
Pull-up or assisted pull-up: 4 sets to 2 reps short of failure.
Barbell or dumbbell row: 4 sets of 8-10.
Lat pulldown: 3 sets of 10-12.
Seated cable row: 3 sets of 10-12, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Face pulls: 3 sets of 15.
Rear delt fly: 3 sets of 15.
Bicep curl: 3 sets of 10-12.
Farmer's carry: 3 x 40 metres heavy, for grip and everything else.
Aim for at least as much pulling volume as pressing across the week (903).
instructions.notes: Pull volume equal to or greater than push volume is what keeps the shoulders healthy.

instructions.title: Core Circuit
instructions.description: Trunk work that actually transfers to sport.
instructions.warnings: Anti-movement — resisting rotation and extension — transfers far better than endless sit-ups.
steps: Plank: 3 x 45-60 seconds. Squeeze the glutes, ribs down, no sagging.
Side plank: 3 x 30-45 seconds each side.
Dead bug: 3 sets of 10 each side, low back pressed to the floor throughout.
Bird dog: 3 sets of 10 each side, slow, no rotation of the hips.
Pallof press: 3 sets of 12 each side, resisting the rotation.
Hollow hold: 3 x 20-30 seconds.
Hanging knee raise or leg raise: 3 sets of 10-12.
Suitcase carry: 3 x 30 metres each side, staying upright.
Rest 45 seconds between exercises, or run it as a circuit with 90 seconds between rounds.

instructions.title: Runner's Strength Routine
instructions.description: The specific strength work that keeps runners uninjured.
instructions.warnings: Single-leg work is the priority. Running is a single-leg sport and two-legged exercises hide imbalances.
steps: Single-leg glute bridge: 3 sets of 12 each side.
Single-leg Romanian deadlift: 3 sets of 10 each side. Slow, controlled, balance is part of it.
Bulgarian split squat: 3 sets of 10 each side.
Step-ups onto a box: 3 sets of 10 each side, driving through the heel.
Side-lying clamshell with a band: 3 sets of 15 each side.
Monster walks with a band: 3 sets of 15 steps each direction.
Calf raises: 3 sets of 15 double-leg, then 3 sets of 12 single-leg.
Single-leg balance: 45 seconds each side, then repeat with eyes closed.
Plank and side plank: 2 sets each (905).
Do this twice a week, ideally on easy run days rather than hard ones.
instructions.notes: Weak glutes are behind a large share of runners' knee and ITB problems. Clamshells are dull and they work.

instructions.title: Kettlebell Circuit
instructions.description: A time-efficient full-body session with one piece of equipment.
instructions.warnings: Stop at pain, as opposed to effort. If you have an injury or a condition that this could affect, get proper advice before starting. Learn the swing properly before loading it. It is a hip hinge, not a squat, and the arms are ropes not levers.
instructions.equipment: One or two kettlebells
steps: Warm up with hip hinges and bodyweight squats, 5 minutes (909).
Kettlebell swing: 5 sets of 15. Snap the hips, bell floats, back stays flat.
Goblet squat: 4 sets of 10.
Single-arm press: 3 sets of 8 each arm.
Single-arm row: 3 sets of 10 each arm.
Turkish get-up: 3 each side, slowly. Excellent and humbling.
Racked carry: 3 x 30 metres each side.
Kettlebell deadlift: 3 sets of 10.
Finish with 3 rounds of 20 swings with 60 seconds rest for conditioning.
Rest 60-90 seconds between sets.
instructions.notes: One kettlebell and a corner of a room is a complete strength programme.

instructions.title: Bodyweight Session (Travel and RV)
instructions.description: A full session needing nothing but floor space.
steps: Warm up: 3 minutes of marching, arm circles and squats (909).
Push-ups: 4 sets to 2 short of failure. Elevate the hands to make them easier, feet to make them harder.
Bodyweight squats: 4 sets of 15-20. Slow down the lowering to make them harder.
Split squats: 3 sets of 12 each leg.
Glute bridge or single-leg glute bridge: 3 sets of 15.
Pike push-ups for the shoulders: 3 sets of 8-12.
Inverted rows under a table, or a band row: 3 sets of 10-12.
Plank: 3 x 45 seconds. Side plank: 2 x 30 seconds each side.
Dead bug: 3 sets of 10 each side.
Calf raises off a step: 3 sets of 20.
Finish with the mobility flow (800).
instructions.notes: Slowing the lowering phase to 4 seconds turns easy bodyweight exercises hard without any equipment.

instructions.title: Warm-Up for Strength Training
instructions.description: The ten minutes before the first working set.
instructions.warnings: Never load a cold joint. The warm-up is not the place to save time.
steps: 5 minutes of general work: rower, bike or brisk walking, until slightly warm.
Leg swings forward and side, 10 each leg.
Hip circles, 10 each direction.
Bodyweight squats, 10, going gradually deeper.
Band pull-aparts, 15.
Shoulder dislocates with a band or stick, 10 (803).
Glute bridges, 15, to wake the glutes before squatting.
Dead bug, 10 each side, to switch the trunk on.
Then ramp the first exercise: empty bar x 10, 40% x 8, 60% x 5, 80% x 3, then the first working set.
Never jump straight to a working weight, however experienced you are.
instructions.notes: The ramp sets are part of the warm-up, not part of the session. Do not count them as volume.
